analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the therapeutic potential of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (hucMSC-sEV) in HPV16-positive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). The research aims to address the lack of effective non-invasive therapies for CIN, a precursor to cervical cancer. Using HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids as a disease model, the study demonstrates that hucMSC-sEV significantly promote squamous differentiation in CIN cells. Mechanistically, the vesicles deliver ceramide synthase 1 (CERS1), upregulating C18 ceramide synthesis and activating non-canonical p53 signaling to drive differentiation. In vivo experiments in NCG mice show that hucMSC-sEV inhibit xenograft growth and modulate differentiation through C18 ceramide metabolism. The findings suggest a novel molecular mechanism and therapeutic strategy for CIN intervention. However, the study is limited to an in vitro and in vivo model, and the results may not fully translate to human clinical settings.

abstract_zh: 宫颈上皮内瘤变 (CIN) 是 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 驱动的 宫颈癌 的前兆,对女性健康构成严重威胁。高危型HPV 感染会导致 CI​​N 进展,但仍缺乏明确的干预目标和有效的非侵入性治疗。在此,我们使用新方法(NAM),特别是 HPV16 阳性宫颈外器官作为人类相关疾病模型,评估了源自人脐带间充质干细胞的工程化无细胞小细胞外囊泡(hucMSC-sEV)的治疗潜力。我们发现hucMSC-sEV显着促进S12细胞和HPV16阳性宫颈外器官的鳞状分化。从机制上讲,该 NAM 平台内的综合多组学分析表明,hucMSC-sEV 传递神经酰胺合酶 1 (CERS1) 上调 C18 神经酰胺 (C18 Cer) 合成,激活非经典 p53 信号传导以驱动鳞状细胞分化。在携带皮下 S12 细胞异种移植物的 NCG 小鼠中,hucMSC-sEV 有效抑制 S12 异种移植物生长,并通过调节 C18 神经酰胺代谢来调节鳞状细胞分化,而这种治疗作用在 CERS1 敲除的 hucMSC-sEV 中被消除。该研究阐明了hucMSC-sEV重塑鞘脂代谢促进宫颈鳞状上皮分化并抑制S12异种移植物发育的分子机制,为CIN干预提供新的潜在靶点和治疗策略。

title: Women's knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding human papillomavirus self-sampling in Poland: a cross-sectional online survey
abstract: Objective Human papillomavirus (HPV)-based screening, including self-sampling, is increasingly recommended, but evidence on Polish women's attitudes toward self-sampling remains scarce. This study assessed knowledge of cervical cancer prevention, screening history, and attitudes toward HPV self-sampling among women in Poland. Methods An anonymous cross-sectional online survey of a 1189 adult women in Poland was conducted between May 2018 and April 2019. The primary outcome was a hypothetical preference for home self-sampling, assuming equivalent diagnostic performance. Participants also rated shame, pain, fear, discomfort, ease, and self-confidence for clinician-collected versus self-collected sampling. Results Of 1189 respondents, 523 (44.00%) stated a preference for self-sampling (67.00% of never-screened vs 36.22% of previously screened women). Previous cytology (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.44, 95% confidence interval [CI] “0.32, 0.62”) and regular gynaecological attendance (aOR 0.35, 95% CI “0.26, 0.46”) were associated with lower preference. Higher education was associated with higher preference (aOR 1.56, 95% CI “1.12, 2.17”). Self-sampling was rated less shameful and uncomfortable, though anticipated pain and fear were slightly higher. Conclusions In this pre-implementation sample, hypothetical interest in HPV self-sampling was considerable, particularly among women outside routine gynaecological care. Clear communication and integration of validated self-sampling within organised screening are warranted.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional online survey in Poland aimed to assess women's knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding HPV self-sampling. The study involved 1189 adult women surveyed between May 2018 and April 2019. Results showed that 44% of respondents preferred self-sampling, with a higher preference among never-screened women (67%) compared to previously screened women (36.22%). Factors associated with lower preference included previous cytology screening and regular gynaecological attendance, while higher education was linked to increased preference. The study suggests that integrating validated self-sampling into organized screening programs could be beneficial, particularly for women not in routine gynaecological care. The evidence is based on a hypothetical preference for self-sampling, assuming equivalent diagnostic performance, and the findings are limited to the survey context without reported limitations.

title: Neoadjuvant Nivolumab plus Carboplatin and Paclitaxel in Patients with Locally Advanced Resectable Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck: A Phase II, Single-Arm Trial.
abstract: Abstract Purpose: In locally advanced resectable squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN), patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy with major pathologic response (MPR) or pathologic complete response (pCR) have overall survival (OS) rates superior to those of patients with poorer pathologic responses. To improve efficacy, we added the PD-1 inhibitor nivolumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy and evaluated the combination. Patients and Methods: In this single-arm, open-label phase II trial, patients with newly diagnosed stage III to IV human papillomavirus (HPV)–negative SCCHN in the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, and larynx or stage II to III HPV-positive oropharyngeal SCCHN received neoadjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel (6 weeks) plus nivolumab (every other week), followed by surgery and adjuvant radiotherapy ± chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was pCR at the primary site. Results: Thirty-four patients were enrolled and received neoadjuvant therapy. Thirty-three patients received surgery (R0 resection = 100%). Disease sites included the oral cavity (79%), oropharynx (12%), hypopharynx (6%), and larynx (3%). Twenty-eight (85%) patients had stage IVA disease. The median postsurgical follow-up was 35.3 months. Fourteen (41%) patients had grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events. Twenty-seven (82%) patients completed all cycles of neoadjuvant therapy. Twenty-four (73%) patients had at least an MPR at the primary site, and 15 (45%) had a pCR. In an unplanned analysis at 3 years, recurrence-free survival and OS were 74% and 83%, respectively. Conclusions: This phase II trial of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel in previously untreated, locally advanced, resectable SCCHN was well tolerated and reached its primary endpoint of pCR at the primary site. A phase III confirmatory study is warranted in advanced-stage, resectable HPV-negative SCCHN. See related commentary by Anderson and Sikora, p.

Patients and methods In this single-arm, open-label phase II trial, patients with newly diagnosed stage III to IV human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative SCCHN in the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, and larynx or stage II to III HPV-positive oropharyngeal SCCHN received neoadjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel (6 weeks) plus nivolumab (every other week), followed by surgery and adjuvant radiotherapy ± chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was pCR at the primary site. Results Thirty-four patients were enrolled and received neoadjuvant therapy. Thirty-three patients received surgery (R0 resection = 100%). Disease sites included the oral cavity (79%), oropharynx (12%), hypopharynx (6%), and larynx (3%). Twenty-eight (85%) patients had stage IVA disease. The median postsurgical follow-up was 35.3 months. Fourteen (41%) patients had grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events. Twenty-seven (82%) patients completed all cycles of neoadjuvant therapy. Twenty-four (73%) patients had at least an MPR at the primary site, and 15 (45%) had a pCR. In an unplanned analysis at 3 years, recurrence-free survival and OS were 74% and 83%, respectively. Conclusions This phase II trial of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel in previously untreated, locally advanced, resectable SCCHN was well tolerated and reached its primary endpoint of pCR at the primary site. A phase III confirmatory study is warranted in advanced-stage, resectable HPV-negative SCCHN. See related commentary by Anderson and Sikora, p.

analysis.research_question_and_background: In locally advanced resectable squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN), patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy with major pathologic response (MPR) or pathologic complete response (pCR) have overall survival (OS) rates superior to those of patients with poorer pathologic responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-arm, open-label phase II trial evaluated neoadjuvant nivolumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel in patients with newly diagnosed stage III to IV human papillomavirus (HPV)–negative SCCHN in the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, and larynx or stage II to III HPV-positive oropharyngeal SCCHN.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that the combination of neoadjuvant nivolumab with carboplatin and paclitaxel achieved a significant pCR rate, which is a novel finding in the treatment of locally advanced resectable SCCHN.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that this combination therapy could improve outcomes for patients with HPV-negative SCCHN, potentially informing future treatment strategies and clinical trials.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was a single-arm trial with no comparator group, which limits the ability to draw definitive conclusions about the efficacy of the treatment.

analysis.summary_en: This phase II trial investigated the efficacy of neoadjuvant nivolumab combined with carboplatin and paclitaxel in patients with locally advanced resectable squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN). The study aimed to improve treatment outcomes by leveraging the PD-1 inhibitor nivolumab. Thirty-four patients were enrolled, with 33 undergoing surgery. The primary endpoint, pathologic complete response (pCR), was achieved in 15 patients (45%). Additionally, 24 patients (73%) had at least a major pathologic response (MPR). The trial was well tolerated, with 41% of patients experiencing grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events. These results suggest that the combination therapy may offer improved outcomes for patients with HPV-negative SCCHN, warranting further investigation in a phase III trial. However, the lack of a comparator group limits the strength of the evidence.

abstract_zh: 摘要 目的:在局部晚期可切除的头颈部鳞状细胞癌(SCCHN)患者中,接受新辅助化疗并获得主要病理反应(MPR)或病理完全反应(pCR)的患者,其总体生存率(OS)优于病理反应较差的患者。为了提高疗效,我们向新辅助化疗中加入了PD-1抑制剂纳武利尤单抗,并评估了联合治疗的效果。患者和方法:本项单臂、开放标签II期试验纳入了新诊断的口腔、口咽、下咽和喉部的局部晚期HPV阴性SCCHN患者,或口咽部II至III期HPV阳性SCCHN患者。患者接受新辅助治疗(卡铂和紫杉醇,6周)联合纳武利尤单抗(每两周一次),随后进行手术和辅助放疗±化疗。主要终点是原发部位的pCR。结果:共纳入34名患者并接受新辅助治疗。33名患者接受了手术(R0切除率为100%)。疾病部位包括口腔(79%)、口咽(12%)、下咽(6%)和喉部(3%)。28名(85%)患者为IV期疾病。术后随访中位数为35.3个月。14名(41%)患者出现3/4级人乳头瘤病毒相关不良事件。27名(82%)患者完成了所有新辅助治疗周期。24名(73%)患者在原发部位至少达到MPR,其中15名(45%)达到pCR。在一项未计划的3年分析中,无病生存率和总体生存率分别为74%和83%。结论:本项II期试验评估了未接受过治疗的局部晚期可切除SCCHN患者的新辅助纳武利尤单抗联合卡铂和紫杉醇治疗,该治疗方案耐受性良好,并达到了原发部位pCR的主要终点。需要在晚期、可切除的HPV阴性SCCHN患者中开展III期确认性研究。参见Anderson和Sikora的评论文章,第p页。

title: HPV-Associated Non-Salivary Adenocarcinoma of the Oropharynx
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated non-salivary adenocarcinoma of the oropharynx is exceptionally rare and poorly defined. We report a multi-institutional series of 12 cases from 6 tertiary centers. Histologic, immunohistochemical, HPV testing, molecular, and follow-up data were reviewed. Among 11 patients with available sex data, all were men; the median age was 62 years (range: 46 to 70 y). The cohort comprised 9 primary oropharyngeal adenocarcinomas and 3 metastatic adenocarcinomas, including a right neck metastasis of presumed oropharyngeal origin and 2 distant metastases in patients with previously documented HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. Primary sites included the palatine tonsil or tonsil-palate region (n=7), base of tongue (n=1), and oropharynx, not otherwise specified (n=1). Among cases with available T-category, 5 of 6 were T3/T4. All tumors showed high-grade adenocarcinoma morphology without a recognizable squamous component, with infiltrative glandular, ductal, or cribriform architecture. Diffuse p16 expression was present in all cases, and high-risk HPV was confirmed by polymerase chain reaction or in situ hybridization. p40 was negative in the tumor cell population in cases 1 to 6, 8, 9, 11, and 12, whereas case 7 showed p40 and CK5/6 expression confined to abluminal cells. Molecular profiling in 2 cases identified alterations or variants involving PIK3CA and PIK3R1 . Follow-up in 6 patients with primary tumors showed distant metastases in 3 and disease-specific death in 1. HPV-associated nonsalivary adenocarcinoma of the oropharynx is a diagnostically challenging tumor that expands the morphologic spectrum of HPV-related oropharyngeal carcinoma. Recognition requires exclusion of salivary-type and metastatic adenocarcinoma and confirmation of HPV association.

analysis.summary_en: This review article focuses on HPV-associated non-salivary adenocarcinoma of the oropharynx, a rare and poorly defined condition. The study reports on a multi-institutional series of 12 cases from 6 tertiary centers, highlighting the demographic and clinical characteristics of the cohort. All tumors exhibited high-grade adenocarcinoma morphology without a squamous component, and diffuse p16 expression was observed in all cases, with high-risk HPV confirmed by PCR or in situ hybridization. The article emphasizes the diagnostic challenges of this condition, noting the need to exclude salivary-type and metastatic adenocarcinomas. Follow-up data showed distant metastases in 3 of 6 patients and one disease-specific death. Molecular profiling identified PIK3CA and PIK3R1 alterations in two cases. The findings suggest that this tumor type expands the morphologic spectrum of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancers and underscores the importance of accurate diagnosis and HPV confirmation.

title: Barriers limiting access to follow-up care after HPV screening for cervical cancer in global settings: A systematic review
abstract: Abstract Follow-up care after a positive human papillomavirus (HPV) screening result is essential for cervical cancer prevention, yet many individuals do not complete diagnostic evaluation or treatment. We conducted a systematic review to synthesize barriers to follow-up care after a positive HPV screening result across diverse international settings. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251062691). We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for English language studies published from 2015 to 2025. Two reviewers independently screened studies, and findings were narratively synthesized. Fifteen studies met inclusion criteria, and were conducted across 12 locations in Africa, Europe, North America, and South America. Five barrier groups emerged: health system barriers (lack of local treatment, long wait times, limited follow-up capacity), knowledge and communication barriers (confusion about HPV results and next steps), psychological and emotional barriers (fear of treatment, stigma surrounding HPV, distrust in medical systems), social and relational barriers (partner influence, gender roles, lack of peer support), and structural and logistical barriers (transportation, costs, work conflicts). Across settings, missed follow-up after positive HPV screening appeared more strongly linked to health-system and structural barriers than lack of motivation. Strengthening referral pathways, patient tracking systems, communication of results, navigation support, and timely treatment access may improve follow-up completion and enhance the effectiveness of HPV-based screening programs.

title_zh: 全球范围内 宫颈癌 HPV 筛查后获得后续护理的障碍:系统评价
source_body_en: Abstract Follow-up care after a positive human papillomavirus (HPV) screening result is essential for cervical cancer prevention, yet many individuals do not complete diagnostic evaluation or treatment. We conducted a systematic review to synthesize barriers to follow-up care after a positive HPV screening result across diverse international settings. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251062691). We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for English language studies published from 2015 to 2025. Two reviewers independently screened studies, and findings were narratively synthesized. Fifteen studies met inclusion criteria, and were conducted across 12 locations in Africa, Europe, North America, and South America. Five barrier groups emerged: health system barriers (lack of local treatment, long wait times, limited follow-up capacity), knowledge and communication barriers (confusion about HPV results and next steps), psychological and emotional barriers (fear of treatment, stigma surrounding HPV, distrust in medical systems), social and relational barriers (partner influence, gender roles, lack of peer support), and structural and logistical barriers (transportation, costs, work conflicts). Across settings, missed follow-up after positive HPV screening appeared more strongly linked to health-system and structural barriers than lack of motivation. Strengthening referral pathways, patient tracking systems, communication of results, navigation support, and timely treatment access may improve follow-up completion and enhance the effectiveness of HPV-based screening programs.

title: Decisional needs for anal cancer screening among high-risk populations: A systematic review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to identify and synthesize decisional needs (i.e., factors that adversely affect decision quality) of anal cancer screening among high-risk populations. METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and PsycINFO were searched from inception years (1946, 1974, 1937, and 1806 respectively) to December 14, 2025. Studies examining anal cancer screening decisional needs among high-risk populations identified by the International Anal Neoplasia Society were eligible. Two reviewers conducted title/abstract, full-text screening and data extraction independently. Study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Directed content analysis was used to synthesize decisional needs by the Ottawa Decision Support Framework. RESULTS: Twenty-two studies involving 6522 participants were included. Twelve cross-sectional and 10 qualitative studies were conducted in the United States, Canada, Australia, and France. The most reported decisional needs were inadequate knowledge (19 studies), inadequate support or resources (15 studies), and unrealistic expectations regarding personal susceptibility to anal cancer or human papillomavirus (seven studies). Knowledge gaps concerned anal cancer risk, screening procedures, and results interpretation. Support needs included insufficient guidance, emotional concerns and limited access. CONCLUSIONS: High-risk populations lack the information and support for anal cancer screening decisions. Implementation should combine tailored risk communication, non-stigmatizing discussion, values clarification, and clear follow-up pathways.

title_zh: 高危人群肛门癌筛查的决策需求:系统评价。
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to identify and synthesize decisional needs (i.e., factors that adversely affect decision quality) of anal cancer screening among high-risk populations. METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and PsycINFO were searched from inception years (1946, 1974, 1937, and 1806 respectively) to December 14, 2025. Studies examining anal cancer screening decisional needs among high-risk populations identified by the International Anal Neoplasia Society were eligible. Two reviewers conducted title/abstract, full-text screening and data extraction independently. Study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Directed content analysis was used to synthesize decisional needs by the Ottawa Decision Support Framework. RESULTS: Twenty-two studies involving 6522 participants were included. Twelve cross-sectional and 10 qualitative studies were conducted in the United States, Canada, Australia, and France. The most reported decisional needs were inadequate knowledge (19 studies), inadequate support or resources (15 studies), and unrealistic expectations regarding personal susceptibility to anal cancer or human papillomavirus (seven studies). Knowledge gaps concerned anal cancer risk, screening procedures, and results interpretation. Support needs included insufficient guidance, emotional concerns and limited access. CONCLUSIONS: High-risk populations lack the information and support for anal cancer screening decisions. Implementation should combine tailored risk communication, non-stigmatizing discussion, values clarification, and clear follow-up pathways.

title: Pre-implementation assessment of upstream domains on the uptake of HPV self-sampling in safety-net settings: a scoping review
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) screening can be used as an early detector for cervical cancer. The newly US Food and Drug Administration-approved HPV self-sampling tests can be used by safety net practices in the USA to help mitigate the current screening disparities seen in patients. As patient acceptability and capability have already been established, this scoping review synthesizes the barriers and facilitators of implementing HPV self-sampling from the perspective of safety net providers and leadership, and the upstream factors not yet explored in current research. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a literature search was conducted exploring peer-reviewed publications and grey literature to establish the current landscape of HPV self-sampling. Findings were organized using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. From the 57 works included, it was found that safety net practices are capable of implementing HPV self-sampling by utilizing current workflows and team members. However, outer setting guidelines and policies heavily influence the implementation process, likely causing a delay in uptake by safety net practices. Recent guideline endorsements and forthcoming insurance coverage address several of these barriers, making post-approval implementation research in safety net settings an urgent priority.

analysis.scope_and_question: This scoping review examines the barriers and facilitators of implementing HPV self-sampling in safety-net settings, focusing on upstream factors that influence its uptake. The review is centered on HPV types and HPV-associated diseases, particularly cervical cancer, and explores the role of provider and leadership perspectives in implementation.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines, conducting a literature search across peer-reviewed publications and grey literature. The findings were organized using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research to identify key implementation factors.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Safety net practices are capable of implementing HPV self-sampling using existing workflows and team members. However, external guidelines and policies significantly influence the implementation process, potentially delaying its adoption in these settings.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is limited evidence on the specific upstream factors affecting HPV self-sampling implementation in safety-net settings. The review highlights the need for further research to address these gaps and understand how policy changes can accelerate uptake.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Post-approval implementation research in safety-net settings is an urgent priority, particularly as recent guideline endorsements and potential insurance coverage may help overcome existing barriers. This research should focus on understanding the impact of policy and external guidelines on implementation success.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review evaluates the barriers and facilitators of implementing HPV self-sampling in safety-net settings, emphasizing upstream factors that influence its adoption. The review identifies that safety-net practices can integrate HPV self-sampling into existing workflows, but external guidelines and policies significantly affect implementation timelines. While patient acceptability and capability are established, the review underscores the need for targeted research to address implementation challenges and leverage recent guideline endorsements and insurance coverage. The findings highlight the importance of understanding how policy changes can support the uptake of HPV self-sampling in underserved populations.

The review is centered on HPV types and HPV-associated diseases, particularly cervical cancer, and explores the role of provider and leadership perspectives in implementation.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines, conducting a literature search across peer-reviewed publications and grey literature. The findings were organized using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research to identify key implementation factors.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Safety net practices are capable of implementing HPV self-sampling using existing workflows and team members. However, external guidelines and policies significantly influence the implementation process, potentially delaying its adoption in these settings.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is limited evidence on the specific upstream factors affecting HPV self-sampling implementation in safety-net settings. The review highlights the need for further research to address these gaps and understand how policy changes can accelerate uptake.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Post-approval implementation research in safety-net settings is an urgent priority, particularly as recent guideline endorsements and potential insurance coverage may help overcome existing barriers. This research should focus on understanding the impact of policy and external guidelines on implementation success.

title_zh: 对安全网环境中 HPV 自我采样情况上游领域的实施前评估:范围界定审查
source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV) screening can be used as an early detector for cervical cancer. The newly US Food and Drug Administration-approved HPV self-sampling tests can be used by safety net practices in the USA to help mitigate the current screening disparities seen in patients. As patient acceptability and capability have already been established, this scoping review synthesizes the barriers and facilitators of implementing HPV self-sampling from the perspective of safety net providers and leadership, and the upstream factors not yet explored in current research. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a literature search was conducted exploring peer-reviewed publications and grey literature to establish the current landscape of HPV self-sampling. Findings were organized using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. From the 57 works included, it was found that safety net practices are capable of implementing HPV self-sampling by utilizing current workflows and team members. However, outer setting guidelines and policies heavily influence the implementation process, likely causing a delay in uptake by safety net practices. Recent guideline endorsements and forthcoming insurance coverage address several of these barriers, making post-approval implementation research in safety net settings an urgent priority.
abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 筛查可用作 宫颈癌 的早期检测器。美国食品和药物管理局新批准的 HPV 自采样检测可供美国的安全网实践使用,以帮助减轻目前患者中出现的筛查差异。由于患者的可接受性和能力已经建立,本次范围审查从安全网提供者和领导层的角度综合了实施 HPV 自我采样的障碍和促进因素,以及当前研究中尚未探讨的上游因素。遵循 PRISMA-ScR 指南,进行了文献检索,探索同行评审的出版物和灰色文献,以确定 HPV 自我采样的当前状况。调查结果是使用实施研究综合框架进行组织的。从纳入的 57 项工作中发现,安全网实践能够利用当前的工作流程和团队成员来实施 HPV 自我采样。然而,外部制定的指导方针和政策严重影响实施过程,可能导致安全网实践的延迟。最近的指南认可和即将推出的保险范围解决了其中一些障碍,使安全网设置的批准后实施研究成为当务之急。

title: TWIST family in cervical cancer biology: From molecular mechanisms to clinical implications.
abstract: Despite ongoing clinical efforts, cervical cancer remains one of the most common gynecologic tumors, largely due to its metastatic potential and resistance to chemotherapy. The transcriptional regulator TWIST has been implicated in these features, in part through the induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The expression of TWIST is delicately regulated by several exogenous factors, including hypoxia-driven HIF-1α signaling and TGF-β pathways, as well as endogenous oncogenic cascades such as Wnt/β-catenin, NF-κB, PI3K/Akt, Hedgehog, Notch, and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3. Moreover, the E6 and E7 proteins from high-risk human papillomavirus strains promote TWIST upregulation, facilitating cellular plasticity and evasion of senescence. Post-transcriptional and epigenetic regulation is orchestrated by complex networks of non-coding RNAs and key transcription factors such as Mist1, FOXC1, and LMX-1A. Importantly, hypermethylation of the TWIST1 promoter has been proposed as a candidate biomarker for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. TWIST has been reported to promote tumor-associated phenotypes through E-cadherin downregulation, induction of matrix metalloproteinases, and maintenance of stem cell-like properties. TWIST has been associated with chemotherapy and radiotherapy resistance, potentially through mechanisms involving DNA-damage responses and MDR1/P-glycoprotein-mediated drug efflux. The tumor microenvironment affects its expression and activity, including hypoxia, cancer-associated fibroblasts, inflammatory cytokines, tumor-associated macrophages, and extracellular vesicles. In a clinical context, high levels of TWIST are linked to poor outcomes in cervical cancer. Growing evidence links it to immune evasion through regulation of PD-L1, immunosuppressive cytokine signaling, macrophage polarization, T-cell exclusion, and immune resistance associated with cancer stem cells, underscoring its importance for translation in the current era of immune checkpoint blockade.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic search methods, databases, or meta-analysis. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while TWIST is implicated in chemotherapy and radiotherapy resistance, the exact mechanisms remain unclear. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that understanding TWIST regulation and its role in cervical cancer could lead to targeted therapies, improved biomarkers for early detection, and better strategies for immune checkpoint blockade in HPV-associated cancers.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the molecular mechanisms and clinical implications of the TWIST family in cervical cancer biology. It highlights the role of TWIST in promoting metastasis, chemotherapy resistance, and immune evasion through processes like EMT and interactions with oncogenic pathways. The review also discusses its regulation by factors such as hypoxia, TGF-β, and HPV proteins, and its potential as a biomarker for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Despite these insights, the exact mechanisms of TWIST-mediated resistance and immune evasion remain unresolved, underscoring the need for further research to inform therapeutic strategies and improve patient outcomes.

abstract_zh: 尽管临床不断努力,宫颈癌 仍然是最常见的妇科肿瘤之一,这主要是由于其转移潜力和对化疗的耐药性。转录调节因子 TWIST 与这些特征有关,部分是通过诱导上皮间质转化 (EMT) 来实现的。TWIST 的表达受到多种外源因子的精细调节,包括缺氧驱动的 HIF-1α 信号传导和 TGF-β 通路,以及内源性致癌级联,例如 Wnt/β-catenin、NF-κB、PI3K/Akt、Hedgehog、Notch 和 IL-6/JAK2/STAT3。此外,来自高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 菌株的 E6 和 E7 蛋白促进 TWIST 上调,促进细胞可塑性和逃避衰老。转录后和表观遗传调控是由非编码 RNA 和关键转录因子(例如 Mist1、FOXC1 和 LMX-1A)组成的复杂网络精心策划的。重要的是,TWIST1 启动子的高甲基化已被提议作为宫颈上皮内瘤变的候选生物标志物。据报道,TWIST 通过下调 E-钙粘蛋白、诱导基质金属蛋白酶和维持干细胞样特性来促进肿瘤相关表型。TWIST 可能通过涉及 DNA 损伤反应和 MDR1/P-糖蛋白介导的药物流出的机制与化疗和放疗耐药性相关。肿瘤微环境影响其表达和活性,包括缺氧、癌症相关成纤维细胞、炎症细胞因子、肿瘤相关巨噬细胞和细胞外囊泡。在临床背景下,高水平的 TWIST 与 宫颈癌 的不良结果相关。越来越多的证据表明,它通过调节 PD-L1、免疫抑制性细胞因子信号传导、巨噬细胞极化、T 细胞排斥以及与癌症干细胞相关的免疫抵抗来逃避免疫,强调了它在当前免疫检查点封锁时代的翻译重要性。

title: Competing Endogenous Ribonucleic Acid Networks in Cervical Cancer: Mechanisms and Clinical Implications.
abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women, with persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) representing its primary etiological factor. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), circular RNAs (circRNAs), and pseudogenes can function as competing endogenous RNAs (ceRNAs) by competing with messenger RNAs (mRNAs) for binding to microRNAs (miRNAs), thereby reducing miRNA-mediated repression of target mRNAs. This review categorizes the ceRNA axes reported in CC as oncogenic or tumor-suppressive and examines their convergence on major signaling pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/Akt, mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), Hippo, and Notch, together with the strength of the supporting evidence. The roles of these networks in prognosis, resistance to cisplatin and radiotherapy, and responses to bioactive compounds are also evaluated. Most reported axes are supported primarily by cell-line experiments, whereas absolute RNA quantification is frequently unavailable and patient-level validation remains limited. Accordingly, ceRNA networks represent potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets, although additional mechanistic and clinical evidence is required to establish their clinical applicability.

abstract_zh: 宫颈癌 (CC) 仍然是女性癌症相关 死亡率 的主要原因,高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV) 的持续感染是其主要病因。长非编码 RNA (lncRNA)、环状 RNA (circRNA) 和假基因可以通过与信使 RNA (mRNA) 竞争与 microRNA (miRNA) 的结合,充当竞争性内源 RNA (ceRNA),从而减少 miRNA 介导的靶 mRNA 抑制。本综述将 CC 中报道的 ceRNA 轴分类为致癌轴或肿瘤抑制轴,并检查了它们在主要信号通路上的收敛性,包括 Wnt/β-连环蛋白、磷酸肌醇 3-激酶 (PI3K)/Akt、丝裂原激活蛋白激酶 (MAPK)、Hippo 和 Notch,以及支持证据的强度。还评估了这些网络在预后、顺铂和放疗耐药性以及对生物活性化合物的反应中的作用。大多数报告的轴主要由细胞系实验支持,而绝对 RNA 定量通常无法实现,并且患者水平的验证仍然有限。因此,ceRNA 网络代表了潜在的生物标志物和治疗靶点,尽管需要额外的机制和临床证据来确定其临床适用性。

title: Global, regional and national burden of cervical cancer in 1990-2023 with forecasts to 2050: a Global Burden of Disease study.
abstract: Although highly preventable, cervical cancer remains one of the most common malignancies among women worldwide. As part of the Global Burden of Disease study, we estimated cervical cancer incidence, mortality and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. In 2023, 887,000 new cases (95% uncertainty interval 682,000-1,170,000), 369,000 deaths (292,000-475,000) and 13.3 million DALYs (10.1-17.4) were estimated globally. Age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) were more than four and seven times higher in low- versus high-income countries. Between 1990 and 2023, global ASIR was largely stable (-0.4% (-26.6 to 34.7)), whereas ASMR changed by -17.5% (-36.2 to 13.4). All cervical cancer DALYs were attributable to human papillomavirus infection, with tobacco use contributing 5.9% (3.2-9.3) globally. By 2050, global ASIR and ASMR are forecast to change by -12.5% (-25.7 to 3.5) and -9.0% (-21.5 to 6.6) from 2024, yet absolute cases and deaths are forecast to rise by 20.2% (4.6-38.5) and 39.3% (23.6-57.3). ASIR and ASMR are forecast to remain highest in low-income countries. Intensified action is needed to accelerate progress.

title: Productive or Transforming? How Epithelial Compartmentalization of HPV DNA and E6/E7 Transcripts Shapes Cervical Screening Assay Performance.
abstract: The human papillomavirus (HPV) life cycle is linked to epithelial cell differentiation, with viral genome amplification, E6/E7 transcription, and virion assembly spatially compartmentalized within the cervical epithelium. This organization is disrupted in transforming lesions. These fundamental observations determine what 'bulk' nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) of cervical exfoliates allow us to establish. DNA-based assays sensitively report high-risk HPV genome presence, which includes transient infections and virus particles. RNA-based assays target the E6/E7 transcripts in transcriptionally active disease, which accounts for their slightly higher clinical specificity for high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions. No single assay defines both viral presence and disease significance, however. Cytology, p16/Ki-67 dual stain, extended genotyping and host-cell methylation interrogate complementary axes of risk with strong biological rationale. The loss of spatial information that limits bulk NAAT approaches matters most in mixed-grade lesions and immunocompromised populations. Emerging spatial methods, AI-assisted cytology and cervical cell-lifts offer recovery of biological resolution.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how the spatial compartmentalization of HPV DNA and E6/E7 transcripts within cervical epithelial cells influences the performance of cervical screening assays.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research focused on the organization of HPV within cervical epithelium, examining its disruption in transforming lesions and its implications for diagnostic methods.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed the spatial distribution of HPV DNA and E6/E7 transcripts, comparing DNA-based assays that detect viral presence with RNA-based assays that target transcriptionally active disease.
analysis.main_results: DNA-based assays sensitively report high-risk HPV genome presence, including transient infections and virus particles, while RNA-based assays have slightly higher clinical specificity for high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the spatial organization of HPV within the epithelium determines the effectiveness of bulk nucleic acid amplification tests, highlighting the need for complementary approaches to capture biological resolution.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of more accurate cervical screening assays by emphasizing the importance of spatial information in assessing HPV-related disease risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges the loss of spatial information in bulk NAAT approaches, which is most critical in mixed-grade lesions and immunocompromised populations, suggesting moderate evidence strength due to its abstract-only nature.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how the spatial compartmentalization of human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA and E6/E7 transcripts within cervical epithelial cells affects the performance of cervical screening assays. It highlights that DNA-based assays are sensitive to HPV presence, including transient infections, while RNA-based assays offer higher specificity for high-grade lesions. The authors emphasize the importance of spatial information in understanding HPV's role in disease, suggesting that complementary methods like cytology, p16/Ki-67 dual stain, and cell-lifts can improve diagnostic accuracy. The study notes limitations in bulk NAAT approaches, particularly in mixed-grade lesions and immunocompromised individuals, and suggests that emerging spatial methods and AI-assisted cytology may recover lost biological resolution. The evidence is abstract-only, providing moderate confidence in its conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解宫颈上皮细胞内 HPV DNA 和 E6/E7 转录本的空间划分如何影响宫颈筛查检测的性能。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究的重点是宫颈上皮内 HPV 的组织,检查其对病变转化的破坏及其对诊断方法的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究分析了 HPV DNA 和 E6/E7 转录本的空间分布,将检测病毒存在的基于 DNA 的检测与针对转录活跃疾病的基于 RNA 的检测进行了比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 基于 DNA 的检测可灵敏地报告 高危型HPV 基因组 的存在,包括短暂感染和病毒颗粒,而基于 RNA 的检测对高级鳞状上皮内病变具有稍高的临床特异性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,上皮内 HPV 的空间组织决定了批量核酸扩增测试的有效性,强调需要补充方法来捕获生物学分辨率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了空间信息在评估 HPV 相关疾病风险中的重要性,为更准确的宫颈筛查测定的开发提供了信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认批量 NAAT 方法会丢失空间信息,这在混合级别病变和免疫功能低下人群中最为关键,这表明由于其仅抽象的性质,证据强度适中。

abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 生命周期与上皮细胞分化相关,病毒 基因组 扩增、E6/E7 转录和病毒体组装在宫颈上皮内空间划分。该组织在病变转化过程中被破坏。这些基本观察结果决定了我们能够对宫颈脱落物进行“大量”核酸扩增测试(NAAT)。基于 DNA 的检测可灵敏地报告 高危型HPV 基因组 的存在,其中包括短暂感染和病毒颗粒。基于 RNA 的检测以转录活跃疾病中的 E6/E7 转录本为目标,这解释了它们对高级鳞状上皮内病变的临床特异性略高。然而,没有单一的检测方法可以同时定义病毒的存在和疾病的重要性。细胞学、p16/Ki-67 双染色、扩展基因分型和 宿主 细胞甲基化以强有力的生物学原理询问风险的互补轴。空间信息的丢失限制了批量 NAAT 方法,这在混合级别病变和免疫功能低下人群中最为重要。新兴的空间方法、人工智能辅助细胞学和宫颈细胞提升术可恢复生物分辨率。

title: Treatment-associated changes in the cervicovaginal microbiome and microbial correlates of HPV clearance and cervical disease outcomes: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract Background Treatment for high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV), cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, and cervical cancer is effective, but HPV may persist or recur. We synthesised evidence on post-treatment cervicovaginal microbiota (CVM) changes and pre-treatment CVM correlates of outcomes. Methods Five databases were searched to August 20, 2026 for studies assessing the CVM molecularly before, or before and after, treatment. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB-2, ROBINS-I, and the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Findings were synthesised narratively under Synthesis Without Meta-analysis guidance and stratified by population, treatment, sampling site, and outcome. Meta-analysis and formal publication-bias assessment were not performed. Results Twenty-one studies were included: 16 cohorts, three non-randomised studies, and two randomised trials. Twenty reported the number of women enrolled ( n = 1,345), whereas one reported 125 vaginal samples without a corresponding number of women. Most excision or probiotic studies reported lower alpha diversity and greater Lactobacillus dominance after treatment; after loop excision, Lactobacillus-depleted communities fell from 32% to 10% among women who cleared HR-HPV in one study. Only five studies included a comparison group. Eight of 11 studies found no baseline alpha-diversity difference by outcome. Baseline Lactobacillus iners was higher with HPV persistence (62% vs 16%; 60% vs 45%); the only adjusted analysis associated it with non-clearance after non-operative management (aOR 3.94, 95% CI 1.06–14.70) but yielded an imprecise estimate after excision (aOR 1.86, 95% CI 0.12–29.42). Individual studies linked several anaerobic taxa to HPV persistence or recurrence and Lacticaseibacillus casei, Peptostreptococcus anaerobius, and Anaerococcus lactolyticus to clearance, but none of these associations was externally validated and multiple-testing correction was inconsistently reported. Conclusions After treatment, the CVM often shifts towards lower-diversity, Lactobacillus-dominant communities, but causality is unproven. iners dominance is a candidate correlate of unfavourable outcomes requiring prospective confirmation.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines treatment-associated changes in the cervicovaginal microbiome and microbial correlates of HPV clearance and cervical disease outcomes. Twenty-one studies were included, with most reporting lower alpha diversity and increased Lactobacillus dominance post-treatment. Baseline Lactobacillus iners was higher in HPV-persistent cases, though associations were not externally validated. The review highlights the need for prospective studies to confirm these findings and explore causal relationships. No meta-analysis was conducted, and the evidence is primarily narrative. The review underscores the importance of understanding microbiome dynamics in HPV-related conditions for future research and clinical practice.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 治疗 宫颈阴道微生物组的相关变化以及 HPV 清除率和宫颈疾病结果的微生物相关性:系统评价。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 截至 2026 年 8 月 20 日,我们检索了五个数据库,以评估 治疗 之前、之前和之后的子宫颈阴道微生物组 (CVM) 分子水平。使用 RoB-2、ROBINS-I 和纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表评估偏倚风险。研究结果在无荟萃分析的综合指导下进行叙述性综合,并按人群、治疗、采样地点和结果进行分层。没有进行荟萃分析和正式的发表偏倚评估。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 纳入 21 项研究:16 项 队列研究、三项非随机研究和两项随机试验。大多数切除或益生菌研究报告称,治疗 后,α 多样性较低,乳酸菌优势较大;一项研究显示,在切除环后,清除 HR-HPV 的女性中,乳酸菌耗尽的群体从 32% 下降到 10%。基线惰性乳杆菌随着 HPV 持续存在而升高(62% vs 16%;60% vs 45%)。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 个别研究将几种厌氧菌类群与 HPV 持续存在或复发联系起来,并将干酪乳杆菌、厌氧消化链球菌和乳酸厌氧球菌与清除联系起来,但这些关联均未经过外部验证,并且多重测试校正的报告也不一致。只有五项研究包括对照组。11 项研究中有 8 项发现基线 α 多样性的结果没有差异。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 基线惰性乳杆菌优势是需要前瞻性确认的不利结果的候选相关性。该综述强调需要进一步研究来验证 HPV 清除率和宫颈疾病结果之间的微生物相关性,并探索微生物组变化与 HPV 持续存在或复发之间的因果关系。

title_zh: 治疗 宫颈阴道微生物组的相关变化以及 HPV 清除率和宫颈疾病结果的微生物相关性:系统评价
source_body_en: Abstract Background Treatment for high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV), cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, and cervical cancer is effective, but HPV may persist or recur. We synthesised evidence on post-treatment cervicovaginal microbiota (CVM) changes and pre-treatment CVM correlates of outcomes. Methods Five databases were searched to August 20, 2026 for studies assessing the CVM molecularly before, or before and after, treatment. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB-2, ROBINS-I, and the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Findings were synthesised narratively under Synthesis Without Meta-analysis guidance and stratified by population, treatment, sampling site, and outcome. Meta-analysis and formal publication-bias assessment were not performed. Results Twenty-one studies were included: 16 cohorts, three non-randomised studies, and two randomised trials. Twenty reported the number of women enrolled ( n = 1,345), whereas one reported 125 vaginal samples without a corresponding number of women. Most excision or probiotic studies reported lower alpha diversity and greater Lactobacillus dominance after treatment; after loop excision, Lactobacillus-depleted communities fell from 32% to 10% among women who cleared HR-HPV in one study. Only five studies included a comparison group. Eight of 11 studies found no baseline alpha-diversity difference by outcome. Baseline Lactobacillus iners was higher with HPV persistence (62% vs 16%; 60% vs 45%); the only adjusted analysis associated it with non-clearance after non-operative management (aOR 3.94, 95% CI 1.06–14.70) but yielded an imprecise estimate after excision (aOR 1.86, 95% CI 0.12–29.42). Individual studies linked several anaerobic taxa to HPV persistence or recurrence and Lacticaseibacillus casei, Peptostreptococcus anaerobius, and Anaerococcus lactolyticus to clearance, but none of these associations was externally validated and multiple-testing correction was inconsistently reported. Conclusions After treatment, the CVM often shifts towards lower-diversity, Lactobacillus-dominant communities, but causality is unproven. iners dominance is a candidate correlate of unfavourable outcomes requiring prospective confirmation.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 治疗 宫颈阴道微生物组的相关变化以及 HPV 清除率和宫颈疾病结果的微生物相关性:系统评价。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 截至 2026 年 8 月 20 日,我们检索了五个数据库,以评估 治疗 之前、之前和之后的子宫颈阴道微生物组 (CVM) 分子水平。使用 RoB-2、ROBINS-I 和纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表评估偏倚风险。研究结果在无荟萃分析的综合指导下进行叙述性综合,并按人群、治疗、采样地点和结果进行分层。没有进行荟萃分析和正式的发表偏倚评估。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 纳入 21 项研究:16 项 队列研究、三项非随机研究和两项随机试验。大多数切除或益生菌研究报告称,治疗 后,α 多样性较低,乳酸菌优势较大;一项研究显示,在切除环后,清除 HR-HPV 的女性中,乳酸菌耗尽的群体从 32% 下降到 10%。基线惰性乳杆菌随着 HPV 持续存在而升高(62% vs 16%;60% vs 45%)。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 个别研究将几种厌氧菌类群与 HPV 持续存在或复发联系起来,并将干酪乳杆菌、厌氧消化链球菌和乳酸厌氧球菌与清除联系起来,但这些关联均未经过外部验证,并且多重测试校正的报告也不一致。只有五项研究包括对照组。11 项研究中有 8 项发现基线 α 多样性的结果没有差异。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 基线惰性乳杆菌优势是需要前瞻性确认的不利结果的候选相关性。该综述强调需要进一步研究来验证 HPV 清除率和宫颈疾病结果之间的微生物相关性,并探索微生物组变化与 HPV 持续存在或复发之间的因果关系。

title: Acceptance and Willingness to Receive HPV Vaccination Among Adult Women Living With HIV and Their Children
abstract: PURPOSE Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a primary preventive strategy for cervical cancer, yet its implementation remains challenging in sub-Saharan Africa. Women living with HIV (WLHIV) are a high-priority group due to their increased risk of persistent HPV infection. This study evaluates the current levels of HPV vaccine awareness and the willingness of WLHIV to accept the vaccine for themselves and their female children in Nigeria. METHODS This multi-center cross-sectional study analyzed data from 4,613 WLHIV across 12 clinical sites. Participants were surveyed on vaccine awareness, personal vaccination history, and future willingness to vaccinate themselves and their children. Logistic regression analysis and Chi-square tests were utilized to determine the relationship between awareness and willingness, applying the Haldane-Anscombe correction for zero-frequency cells where appropriate. RESULTS Awareness was critically low; only 10.4% (n = 481) of participants had ever heard of the HPV vaccine. This deficit in literacy directly influenced behavioral outcomes: only 8.2% (n = 378) were willing to receive the vaccine personally, 0.6% (n = 26) declined, and 0.6% (n = 26) were uncertain. Willingness to vaccinate female children was even lower, with only 1.1% (n = 50) indicating acceptance, while the vast majority had no recorded response. A crucial finding was the absolute correlation between knowledge and intent, as zero (0%) women who were unaware of the vaccine expressed willingness to receive it. In contrast, awareness was a near-perfect predictor of acceptance ( P < .001). The primary reported barriers were a lack of information on vaccine availability, concerns about the cost of the vaccine, a lack of recommendations from healthcare providers, and uncertainty about where to access vaccination services. CONCLUSION The findings reveal a profound deficit in vaccine literacy among Nigerian WLHIV. The near-total absence of willingness in the absence of awareness confirms that literacy is the fundamental gateway to uptake. Public health strategies must prioritize intensive, provider-led educational interventions and normalize HPV vaccination within routine HIV care to overcome current levels of hesitancy and improve multi-generational cancer prevention.

title: Improving HPV Vaccine Uptake Among Girls Aged 9–14 Years in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria: A Community-Participatory Pre/Post-Intervention Study
abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women in Nigeria, where Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine uptake has historically been among the lowest in sub-Saharan Africa. Despite the introduction of the HPV vaccine into Nigeria's National Immunisation Programme in 2023, uptake remains suboptimal. This study evaluated the effect of a community-participatory, multi-channel sensitisation intervention on HPV vaccine uptake, awareness, and knowledge among caregivers of girls aged 9–14 years in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. Methods A pre/post-intervention study was conducted across six communities in three local government areas representing urban, semi-urban, and rural settings. Independent cross-sectional surveys were administered to caregivers of eligible girls before (n = 331, January 2025) and after (n = 355, June 2025) a fourteen-week community sensitisation intervention delivered through five channels: churches, schools, primary healthcare facilities, community sound announcers, and physical materials. All materials were co-designed with community stakeholders. Descriptive statistics, chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests, and multivariable logistic regression were used for analysis. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results HPV vaccine uptake increased from 7.3% (95% CI: 4.5%–10.0%) to 50.4% (95% CI: 45.2%–55.6%), an absolute increase of 43.1 percentage points. HPV vaccine awareness rose from 15.1% to 65.4% (p < 0.001). Among HPV-aware respondents, good HPV knowledge increased from 63.9% to 84.3% (p = 0.019), though vaccine-specific knowledge remained predominantly poor across both phases (4.0% vs. Willingness to vaccinate among unvaccinated caregivers was high and unchanged (87.0% vs. Routine facility records corroborated survey findings, showing a 276% increase in mean monthly doses administered. HPV vaccine awareness was the strongest independent predictor of uptake in both phases (pre-intervention aOR 9.88, 95% CI: 2.07–47.46; post-intervention aOR 16.59, 95% CI: 6.98–39.46). Conclusions A community co-designed, multi-channel sensitisation intervention was associated with a substantial increase in HPV vaccine uptake within six months. Limited awareness rather than vaccine hesitancy was the primary barrier in this setting. Sustaining these gains requires parallel investment in vaccine supply-chain resilience alongside community sensitisation, and future interventions should prioritise strengthening vaccine-specific knowledge to support informed and durable vaccination uptake. Trial registration Pan African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR), PACTR202609683563072, [07 September, 2026]. Retrospectively registered.

title: Factors influencing parental hesitancy toward HPV vaccination in Sub-Saharan Africa: a scoping review
abstract: Background The prevalence of cervical cancer is highest in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), yet the region’s coverage of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is still low and varies greatly between and within nations. HPV vaccination targets adolescents, making parental and caregiver consent and decision-making essential to vaccination program success. Parental hesitancy is a major determinant of whether national vaccination programs result in population-level protection, and a range of factors have been identified as drivers of parental reluctance. Objectives This scoping review aims to map and synthesize the evidence on factors influencing parental hesitancy toward HPV vaccination in Sub-Saharan Africa, including individual, household, sociocultural, informational, and health-system determinants, while identifying gaps for future research. Methods An initial multi-database search (PubMed/MEDLINE, SpringerLink, ProQuest and ScienceDirect; May to June 2026) identified 236 records, of which 79 unique records were screened and 36 studies met the eligibility criteria. An updated search with expanded terms was then run in PubMed, ScienceDirect and SpringerLink and a new database, AJOL; (200 records), which added 22 eligible studies, giving 58 studies in total. Hesitancy was defined as delay in acceptance or refusal of vaccination despite service availability; studies of acceptance, willingness, knowledge, attitudes or perceptions were eligible when they also reported determinants of hesitancy. Data were charted and synthesized narratively. Results The 58 included studies spanned ten Sub-Saharan African countries namely Nigeria, Cameroon, South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Malawi, and Zambia, published between 2016 and 2026, and comprised cross-sectional surveys, qualitative studies, mixed-methods studies, a randomized survey experiment, quasi-experimental studies, and programmatic/stakeholder assessments. Recurring factors included wide variation in HPV/cervical cancer awareness, safety and side-effect concerns (including fears of infertility and conspiracy beliefs), cost and geographic access barriers, religious and cultural beliefs, the paradoxical relationship between caregiver education and hesitancy, and the influence of health workers, social media, and community/religious leaders. Conclusion Parental hesitancy toward HPV vaccination across Sub-Saharan Africa is shaped by overlapping informational, sociocultural, economic, and trust-related factors that vary substantially by country, delivery platform, and rollout maturity. Closing the region’s HPV vaccination gap may require country and community-tailored, multicomponent strategies combining trusted-messenger communication, dedicated safety-concern counseling, and continued attention to cost and access barriers, particularly in under-studied countries and rural settings.

title: Beyond the Adolescent Window: HPV Vaccination in Adult Women
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination has traditionally targeted girls and adolescents before sexual debut, when its preventive potential is greatest. However, many women reach adulthood unvaccinated or incompletely vaccinated, a gap widened by the COVID-19 pandemic. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence on HPV vaccination in adult women and its implications for gynecological practice. Sexual debut, previous infection, or a positive HPV test does not preclude benefit, because few women have been exposed to all vaccine types; nevertheless, the vaccine is prophylactic and does not treat established infection or lesions. In women aged 27 to 45 years, trials show favorable immunogenicity, efficacy, and safety, and vaccination is recommended through shared clinical decision-making that considers prior exposure and the risk of new exposures. Evidence above 45 years of age remains scarce. After excisional treatment of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse, meta-analyses predominantly based on observational studies suggest lower recurrence rates following adjuvant vaccination, although this benefit has not been consistently confirmed by randomized controlled trials. We also discuss additional vaccination with the nonavalent vaccine after bivalent or quadrivalent series, single-dose schedules, people living with HIV, and cervical screening in vaccinated women, in whom HPV-based testing maintains better performance than cytology. Missed opportunities remain common, and the absence of a recommendation from a health care professional is among the main reasons adults remain unvaccinated. Reviewing vaccination history at every gynecological visit, combined with individualized counseling, may help close the gap between vaccinated young cohorts and unvaccinated adult women and support cervical cancer elimination goals.

title: Impact of cervical cancer education on knowledge, attitudes and preventive practices among adolescent girls in secondary schools: a scoping review
abstract: Background Cervical cancer remains one of the most preventable yet deadliest cancers affecting women in Africa. Despite global advances in prevention through human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, screening, and early treatment, Sub-Saharan Africa continues to experience disproportionately high incidence and mortality rates because of limited health infrastructure, inadequate awareness, and delayed diagnosis. Given that adolescence represents a critical window for establishing lifelong health behaviors, school-based cervical cancer education may provide an effective platform for improving knowledge and promoting preventive practices in line with the World Health Organization’s (WHO) cervical cancer elimination strategy. Methods This review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and reported following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, African Journals Online (AJOL), the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was undertaken for studies published up to 2026. A total of 1,700 records were identified and screened, resulting in the inclusion of 20 eligible studies. Data were extracted, charted, and synthesized using a narrative approach. Results Evidence suggests that baseline knowledge of cervical cancer and HPV among adolescent girls in African secondary schools remains generally low to moderate. A consistent knowledge-attitude gap was identified, whereby positive attitudes toward prevention frequently coexisted with limited factual understanding of cervical cancer risk factors, screening, and HPV vaccination. Educational interventions, including peer-led programmes, classroom-based teaching, health campaigns, and multimodal educational strategies, consistently produced significant improvements in knowledge and awareness. However, improvements were less pronounced for more complex concepts, including disease curability, recommended screening intervals, and vaccine mechanisms. Furthermore, an intention-behavior gap was observed, as high levels of vaccine acceptance rarely translated into actual uptake because of parental, sociocultural, and health system barriers. Geographical analysis revealed a substantial concentration of studies in a limited number of Anglophone countries, particularly Nigeria, Ghana, Ethiopia, Kenya, and Uganda, highlighting important gaps in evidence across many African settings. Conclusion School-based cervical cancer education represents a feasible and scalable strategy for improving cervical cancer literacy among African adolescents. However, achieving the WHO’s cervical cancer elimination targets will require a shift from isolated educational sessions toward sustainable, curriculum-integrated, multilevel interventions involving schools, families, healthcare providers, and policymakers. Future research should prioritize the evaluation of long-term behavioral outcomes, particularly HPV vaccine uptake and participation in cervical cancer screening programmes.

title: Serology-Anchored Comparison of Self-Reported Vaccination: Reported Hepatitis B Series Completion Exceeds Vaccine-Consistent Immunity in the Same Participants
abstract: A large secondary literature draws adult vaccination status from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), whose accuracy is rarely quantified alongside it. The objective of this article is to quantify that accuracy in the same participants, because its size and direction decide whether these items can support a coverage claim. The methods we used pooled ten NHANES cycles (1999–2018, adults ≥ 20 years; analytic n 13,992–48,959 by vaccine) and compared self-reported, completed-series uptake with a within-person biological reference. That reference exists for hepatitis B in 2015–2016 only and does not validate the hepatitis A or human papillomavirus (HPV) estimates. Our results are that among the 4473 respondents with both measures, self-reported vaccination rates (33.5%, 95% CI: 30.5–36.5%) stood 10.9 percentage points (7.5–14.3) above vaccine-consistent serology (22.6%, 19.9–25.2%), a ratio of 1.48 (1.30–1.67). They disagreed in both directions, 845 reporting the series without the serologic profile and 294 carrying the profile without reporting it, so the difference is not a measure of over-reporting. Tested directly, it was a near-constant multiple across sex, age, and race. Published National Health Interview Survey coverage, matched on dose definition, population, and year, gave ratios up to 3.00. Four adjusted estimators placed the effect of a usual source of care at 5.7–6.5 percentage points for hepatitis B and 2.5–3.2 for HPV, three excluding zero and the causal forest’s wider interval covering it. The conclusions drawn are that the two measures are not interchangeable and that NHANES figures should be read as reported uptake, not coverage surveillance.

title: Analysis of HPV Genotype Distribution, Viral Load Profiles, and Their Relationship With Cervical Pathology Among Women in Samarkand Region (2023-2025)
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Persistent infection with high-risk oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary cause of cervical cancer development. Objective To evaluate the prevalence of various HPV genotypes, describe genotype-specific viral load patterns, and determine their relationship with patient age and cervical cytological changes among women in the Samarkand region. Methods In a cross-sectional study (2023–2025), cervical epithelial samples from 535 women (aged 19–56 years) were analyzed. Genotyping of 21 HPV types and quantification of viral load (expressed in \(\:\text{l}\text{g}\) copies of DNA/105 cells) were performed using real-time PCR. Cytological status was classified according to The Bethesda System (TBS, 2014) in cohorts with monoinfection (n = 73) and mixed infection (n = 20). Results Out of 116 HPV-positive cases, HPV 16 was unconditionally dominant (24%). An atypically low prevalence of HPV 18 (3%) was observed alongside a high detection rate of non-vaccine types: HPV 56 (6%), 51 (5%), and 58 (4%). No statistically significant correlation was found between patient age and viral load (p > 0.05). A significant overall association was revealed between HPV genotype and cytological status (χ2=97.06; df = 68; p = 0.012). HPV 58 demonstrated the highest pathogenetic potential (OR = 12.11; 80% of cases were ASC-US, 20% were ASC-H) and was never detected in normal cytology (NILM). No direct linear correlation was found between viral load level and lesion severity: peak loads were recorded in NILM cases, whereas the only severe case (HSIL, associated with HPV 68) presented with a low viral load (2.7 lg copies/105 cells). Conclusion The regional epidemiological profile is determined by the dominance of HPV 16 and a high circulation of high-risk non-vaccine strains (56, 51, 58). Viral load exhibits immense genotype-specific variability and does not directly correlate with the severity of cytological changes, highlighting the necessity of integrating multi-genotype PCR testing and cytological screening.

HPV 58 demonstrated the highest pathogenetic potential (OR = 12.11; 80% of cases were ASC-US, 20% were ASC-H) and was never detected in normal cytology (NILM). title: Gastric-type adenocarcinoma of the cervix masquerading as serous endometrial carcinoma: a diagnostic pitfall
abstract: Introduction and importance: Gastric-type adenocarcinoma (GAC) of the cervix is a rare, aggressive, human papillomavirus (HPV)-independent subtype of endocervical adenocarcinoma that can closely resemble other high-grade gynecologic malignancies, particularly serous endometrial carcinoma. Accurate diagnosis is essential because GAC is associated with adverse outcomes and can be difficult to classify when it extends into the lower uterine segment. Presentation of case: A 67-year-old postmenopausal woman presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and a diffusely enlarged cervix. Endometrial sampling initially suggested high-grade serous carcinoma arising in an endometrial polyp, while magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a 5.5-cm mass centered in the cervix with lower uterine segment extension and no radiologic lymphadenopathy. She underwent a type II modified radical hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy, and pelvic lymph-node dissection. Final pathology showed a 6-cm HPV-independent GAC involving all four cervical quadrants, with 15-mm deep stromal invasion, focal lymphovascular space invasion, perineural invasion, and lower uterine segment extension; parametria and vaginal cuff were uninvolved, and the paracervical margin was negative but <1 mm. Two pelvic lymph nodes were negative. The tumor was high-risk HPV negative, p16 focally positive (non-block), PAX8 diffusely positive, p53 wild-type, ER diffusely positive, PR negative, and MMR proficient. MUC6 and HIK1083 were unavailable. The tumor was classified as FIGO 2018 stage IB3. Postoperative concurrent chemoradiotherapy was initiated 4 weeks after surgery without a brachytherapy boost. At 14 months after surgery, the patient remained disease-free. Clinical discussion: This case illustrates a diagnostic pitfall in which cervical GAC mimicked serous endometrial carcinoma because of lower uterine segment involvement, papillary high-grade morphology, and an endometrial polyp. The cervical epicenter, barrel-shaped enlargement, deep cervical stromal invasion, HPV negativity, focal/non-block p16 expression, wild-type p53 pattern, and integrated histologic review supported a cervical gastric-type primary. Gastric differentiation markers are useful supportive tests when available, but MUC6 and HIK1083 were not available in this case, and this limitation is explicitly acknowledged. Conclusion: GAC of the cervix is a rare HPV-independent malignancy in which accurate localization of the primary site is as important as immunophenotypic interpretation. Careful correlation of gross findings, imaging, histology, HPV status, and immunohistochemistry can prevent misdiagnosis as serous endometrial carcinoma and guide multidisciplinary treatment.

title: The potential role of infections in melanoma
abstract: Introduction Several infectious agents have been implicated in the development of human cancers; however, whether infections contribute to the etiology of melanoma remains unclear. This review evaluated the available evidence regarding potential infectious causes of melanoma. The objective is to determine the evidence available regarding the associations of infectious agents with the development of melanoma. Methods A scoping review of the literature was conducted to identify studies investigating the links between infectious agents and melanoma. Four databases were searched using a combination of keywords and controlled vocabulary for published academic articles. Based on the inclusion criteria, 791 titles and abstracts were screened, and 22 articles were obtained. Inclusion criteria were for studies examining associations between viral infectious agents and melanoma; no language restrictions; and no date range restrictions. The review was broadly inclusive of study types including epidemiologic studies such as meta-analyses, systematic and narrative reviews and observational studies; laboratory and mechanistic studies; and case reports. Studies were grouped into three categories: epidemiologic studies evaluating direct associations between infections and melanoma; laboratory and mechanistic studies investigating potential infection-related carcinogenic pathways for melanoma; and studies examining infections that may predispose to cancers overall, including melanoma. Appropriate-for-study-design criteria were applied to each group of studies to assess and summarize their quality. Results Twenty-two studies met inclusion criteria and were determined to be of moderate to high quality. Infectious agents investigated included human papillomavirus (HPV), Human Herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8), herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2), Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and the cutaneous microbiome. Three epidemiologic studies directly examined the relationship between infections and melanoma; however, complete study data were available for only one study. These studies had inconsistent results. Seven laboratory and experimental studies demonstrated biologically plausible pathways through which infectious agents, particularly human papillomavirus (HPV) and herpes simplex virus (HSV), may contribute to carcinogenesis. However, the most evidence for biological plausibility was from studies of general cancer biology or non-melanoma skin cancers. Studies examining infections as potential cancer-predisposing conditions generally were the most abundant (12 of 22 studies) and consistently identified HIV-associated immunosuppression as a risk factor for cancers, including increased melanoma incidence and poorer outcomes. Conclusion The available evidence is currently insufficient to determine whether infectious agents are direct causes of melanoma. There are very few epidemiologic studies assessing the associations of infections and melanoma specifically, and these studies demonstrate inconsistent results. Available laboratory and mechanistic studies show biological plausibility for infectious contributions to melanoma-related carcinogenesis; however, direct evidence supporting specific roles in melanoma development remains limited. The largest numbers of studies available have identified that infections such as HIV and their associated immunosuppression that influence cancer risk overall, also influence melanoma risk, indirectly through immune dysfunction. Some available descriptive surveillance databases have shown increased melanoma rates among occupational groups at increased risk of person-to-person infection transmission exposure. Thus, more epidemiologic and laboratory studies are needed to investigate the potential role of infections in melanomas specifically.

title: Parent-Directed Hesitancy-Addressing Strategies in School-Based HPV Vaccination Programs: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Effects on Vaccine Uptake Among School-Aged Girls
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is safe and effective in preventing cervical and other HPV-related cancers, yet coverage remains below public health targets in many countries. School-based vaccination programmes provide an important platform for reaching large numbers of adolescents. However, vaccination uptake often depends on parental consent and support, as parents play a central role in vaccination decision-making for school-aged children. Parental concerns about vaccine safety, perceived necessity, potential effects on sexual behaviour, and trust in vaccine-related information are widely reported barriers to HPV vaccine acceptance and uptake. To address these barriers, school-based HPV vaccination programmes may incorporate parent-directed components designed to address parental concerns and facilitate informed vaccination decisions. Such approaches may include tailored education and recommendations, vaccine safety and risk communication, misinformation correction, decision-support tools, provider–parent counselling, and digital communication. These strategies target different cognitive, emotional, and interpersonal determinants of parental vaccine hesitancy, and may be delivered individually or as part of multicomponent interventions. Understanding the relative contributions of these approaches is important for identifying effective strategies to improve actual vaccination uptake. title: HPV vaccination uptake among adolescent girls in Nigeria: A multi-state pilot trial using linked mother-daughter data.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nigeria's human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rollout creates opportunities to strengthen adolescent vaccination through participatory, family-engaged approaches. We examined HPV vaccination uptake and associated characteristics among adolescent girls in a multi-state pilot using linked mother-daughter data. METHODS: We analyzed pilot data from 331 vaccine-naïve girls aged 9-14 years, 325 mothers/guardians, and 326 linked mother-daughter records across seven Nigerian states. The participatory approach combined community engagement, maternal HPV DNA self-sampling, and school- and community-linked access to routine HPV vaccination. The primary outcome was logbook-verified vaccination uptake. Exploratory associations were assessed using log-binomial generalized estimating equations to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Of 331 girls, 314 (94.9%) received HPV vaccination, with complete outcome ascertainment. No vaccine-related serious adverse events were recorded. In exploratory adjusted analyses, uptake was higher among Igbo girls (aRR 1.13, 95% CI 1.06-1.22) and girls of other ethnicities (aRR 1.10, 95% CI 1.01-1.19) than among Yoruba girls. Maternal income was positively associated with uptake (aRR per income category 1.02, 95% CI 1.01-1.03). Associations involving maternal screening participation require caution because few mothers did not participate in screening. CONCLUSIONS: HPV vaccination uptake was high among girls participating in this pilot. The exploratory findings suggest areas for further investigation but cannot establish intervention effectiveness or causal relationships. Larger studies should evaluate implementation processes, comparative effectiveness, and equity. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06728085.

title: Building HPV Vaccine Confidence with and for Healthcare Workers in Nigeria: A Co-Design Study
abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer, primarily caused by human papillomavirus (HPV), is a global public health concern, particularly affecting women in low- and middle-income countries, including Nigeria. The HPV vaccine prevents cervical cancer, yet uptake remains low due to supply and confidence barriers. While vaccine confidence among women and girls, and their families has received wide attention, less attention has focused on healthcare workers (HCWs), despite their key role in improving uptake. Co-designing interventions with HCWs could yield better-tailored programs addressing context-specific communication and information needs. Here, we describe the co-design process with HCWs in Nigeria, the strategies and delivery mechanisms identified, and provide methodological reflections. Methods We conducted a co-design study guided by human-centred design and the Ideate, Design, Evaluate, and Share (IDEAS) framework, in Oyo and Jigawa states, Nigeria, between September 2024 and September 2025. Co-design participants included doctors, nurses, and community health extension workers, recruited using purposive and snowball sampling. Data were collected through participatory workshops using audio recordings, field notes, and visuals of co-produced materials, and analysed using content analysis, with findings iteratively refined and validated with participants across workshops. Results Through a series of five workshops and three rounds of sense checks involving 45 HCWs, participants identified gaps in access to HPV vaccine knowledge, difficulty addressing rumours, and a lack of confidence in counselling. In response, we jointly developed content for intervention approaches: in-person and digital. The in-person intervention is planned to be delivered in the health facility by a trained HPV champion. The digital intervention in planned to be delivered through WhatsApp. Both use four short educational videos, which were co-designed with the HCWs, to increase HCWs’ knowledge and confidence in the HPV vaccine, covering: 1) general knowledge on cervical cancer, HPV, and HPV vaccine; 2) counselling parents on HPV vaccine, and 3) strategies for addressing rumours around the HPV vaccine. Conclusion The co-design study enabled successful development of co-designed videos, and in-person and digital intervention delivery strategies to strengthen HPV vaccine confidence among HCWs in Nigeria.

title: Rationale and design of randomized, double-blind trial evaluating the efficacy of single-dose HPV vaccine efficacy in women aged 18 to 30: The PRISMA trial.
abstract: Evidence from the Costa Rica HPV Vaccine Trial suggested that a single dose may provide durable protection in young adult women. Subsequent studies confirmed the non-inferiority of one vs. two doses of the main vaccines among young girls. Vaccination of older cohorts might accelerate cervical cancer elimination, especially if a single dose provides adequate protection. Randomized data are needed to support extended-age, single-dose vaccination strategies. Herein, we present the design, rationale and recruitment results of a three-arm, randomized, double-blinded, clinical trial in Costa Rica to evaluate the efficacy of a single dose of the bivalent (Cervarix®) and nonavalent (Gardasil 9®) HPV vaccines compared with an active control (Tdap). 4925 HPV vaccine-naïve women aged 18-30 years old were enrolled, randomized 1:1:1, and followed for 36 months with cervicovaginal self-sampling every six months starting at 12 months, annual blood collection, and oral/anal sampling at selected visits, with high participation rates. Participants attended ~90% of planned study visits and >96% of attendees provided the necessary specimens. The primary endpoint is incident cerviccovaginal HPV16/18 infection persisting ≥6 months among women HPV16/18 DNA-negative at the enrollment and vaccination visits. Secondary endpoints include vaccine efficacy in the intention-to-treat cohort, oral and anal HPV16/18 protection, and immunogenicity profiles. Trial results will inform mathematical models estimating impact and cost-effectiveness of extending single-dose vaccination to adult young women and directly inform policy to enable extended-age, single-dose strategies to accelerate cervical cancer prevention globally. Furthermore, the study will provide the first evidence for single-dose efficacy against anal and oral HPV infection.
