title: Community Determinants Shaping Readiness for Mobile Cervical Cancer Test-and-Treat Services in Mali and Nigeria
abstract: PURPOSE Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of preventable morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), driven by numerous structural and cultural factors, including limited access to and acceptance of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) screening. Mobile test-and-treat models offer a promising strategy to expand access in rural settings, yet successful implementation requires strong community readiness and engagement. We conducted a pre-implementation assessment to identify community-level determinants influencing readiness, acceptability, and feasibility of mobile hrHPV screening in Mali and Nigeria. METHODS A mixed-methods study was conducted in four communities in Nigeria and two communities in Mali; intended sites for a mobile van hrHPV test-and-treat intervention. Guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research, we administered quantitative surveys and conducted qualitative focus group discussion with political, religious, and civic leaders and with women aged 25-65 in each community. Quantitative data were summarized descriptively. Qualitative data were collaboratively coded by partners in Mali, Nigeria, and the United States. Cross-site matrices were used to compare implementation barriers, facilitators, and readiness indicators across communities and stakeholder groups. RESULTS Community readiness for mobile hrHPV screening varied across sites. Leaders consistently expressed strong support for mobile services but emphasized the need for structured community mobilization, trusted local messengers, and culturally appropriate communication strategies. Women reported enthusiasm for accessible screening while also expressing concerns related to stigma, fear of positive results, and misconceptions about HPV and cervical cancer. Communities with prior exposure to HPV vaccination or mobile health programs demonstrated higher trust, fewer misconceptions, and greater anticipated uptake. Structural barriers, including travel distance, competing responsibilities, and limited engagement with preventive health services, were more pronounced in lower-readiness communities. CONCLUSION Pre-implementation assessments are critical to the success of mobile HPV screening programs in LMICs. Findings highlight the importance of tailored community engagement, targeted health literacy strategies, and alignment with existing community structures to improve acceptability, equity, and scalability of mobile hrHPV test-and-treat services in Mali and Nigeria.

title: Cervicovaginal microbiome modulates HPV genotype-specific clearance/persistence: role of bacterial dysbiosis in cervical carcinogenesis
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study focuses on the distinct epidemiological features of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) genotypes in Asian populations: HPV52/56/58 show uniquely high prevalence and strong correlation with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, but their detection rates drop sharply in invasive cervical cancer, a pattern clearly different from the persistent dominance of HPV16/18 throughout malignant progression. METHODS: To further elucidate the potential host-microbe interactions underlying these epidemiological observations, we integrated a 16S rRNA-sequenced cross-sectional discovery cohort and an independent longitudinal validation cohort from a Chinese population, with strict experimental quality control throughout the workflow. RESULT: The preliminary analytical results demonstrate that a Lactobacillus-dominant cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) is significantly and positively associated with HPV viral clearance, while enriched abundance of Gardnerella, Saccharofermentans and Atopobium exhibits a robust correlation with persistent HPV52/56/58 infection. Three undercharacterized microbial taxa-Chryseobacterium, Sphingobacterium and Enhydrobacter are closely linked to sustained HPV16/18 prevalence across advanced disease stages, and show negative correlation with the above obligate anaerobes, which aligns with the sharp decline of HPV52/56/58 in tumor tissues. A hormone-linked Chryseobacterium enrichment were also identified, a taxon with previously reported progesterone-degrading functional properties. CONCLUSION: While further longitudinal studies are required to establish causal relationships, our results indicate that CVM dysbiosis may modulate the natural history of these high-burden HPV genotypes, and provide a foundational rationale for subsequent development of genotype-specific, microbiota-targeted cervical disease intervention strategies.

title: Successful eradication of Candida auris in a tertiary care ICU following a nearly 30 month outbreak: a drastic "Unit reset" protocol.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Candida auris is a globally emerging, multidrug-resistant pathogen characterized by extreme environmental persistence and resistance to standard hospital disinfectants. Our ICU faced an endemic outbreak that lasted for 30 months, which was resistant to standard infection prevention and control (IPC) bundles. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of a radical, multi-sectoral "Unit Reset" protocol involving total operational decanting, mechanical disassembly, and inventory disposal after incremental IPC strategies were exhausted. METHODS: We executed a 120-hour "Unit Reset" in February 2026. The intervention comprised: (1) transferring all patients to a temporary satellite site; (2) total disposal of all pharmaceutical and disposable inventories; (3) structural remediation; and (4) dual-team mechanical disinfection with 5,000 ppm hypochlorite supplemented by 18% automated hydrogen peroxide vapor (HPV). RESULTS: Over the 30-month endemic period, C. auris acquisition rates escalated despite high compliance with standard IPC bundles. Environmental surveillance rounds identified persistent reservoirs on high-touch surfaces that the routine cleaning protocols missed. Following the 120-hour Unit Reset, the ICU was reopened to admissions. During the subsequent 16-week active surveillance window, zero new clinical acquisitions or screening-positive cases were detected, representing the first sustained interruption of transmission since August 2023. CONCLUSIONS: When C. auris achieves deep environmental sequestration within deteriorated medical infrastructure or complex equipment housings, incremental "enhanced cleaning" protocols may fail due to biofilm shielding. A radical, coordinated institutional reset can terminate entrenched nosocomial transmission when standard IPC bundles reach their limits.

title: Cervical cancer awareness among Namibian women: Perspectives of primary healthcare nurses.
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health concern in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Namibia, where high rates of HIV and HPV infections and early sexual activity increase its prevalence. Limited awareness of cervical cancer among Namibian women contributes significantly to delayed screening and treatment, reducing the likelihood of successful outcomes. This qualitative study explored the perceptions and experiences of 73 professional nurses purposively selected from public primary healthcare facilities across Namibia's fourteen regions. Data were collected through focus group discussions and analysed thematically, with an independent coder to ensure rigor. Findings revealed a substantial lack of awareness among women, highlighting the need for nurses to lead educational initiatives. The study advocates empowering nurses to strengthen patient-nurse relationships and implement community-based awareness programs, including media outreach to isolated populations. It contributes to public health knowledge by emphasizing strategies to promote prevention, early diagnosis, and improved cervical cancer outcomes in Namibia.

title: Global Disparities in Vaccine Reimbursement for Adults Living with HIV: A Cross-Sectional Survey of 120 Countries by EVASG and ESTISG
abstract: Abstract Objective Adults living with HIV are at increased risk of vaccine-preventable infections, yet access to recommended vaccines varies globally. We evaluated national vaccination guidelines, public reimbursement, and on-site vaccination availability across countries with different income levels. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional survey of HIV clinicians and experts representing 120 countries. The 26-item questionnaire assessed vaccination guidelines, recommendations, public reimbursement, and on-site vaccination availability. Countries were classified according to World Bank income group. Generalized linear mixed-effects models assessed routine recommendations, full reimbursement, and recommendation-reimbursement gaps by vaccine type and income group. Results A total of 124 responses representing 120 countries were analyzed, including 38 low-/lower-middle-income (LIC/LMIC), 36 upper-middle-income (UMIC), and 50 high-income countries (HIC). HIV-specific national vaccination guidelines were reported by 37% of respondents, increasing from 18% in LIC/LMIC to 52% in HIC ( p =0.026). Only 30% reported full public reimbursement for all recommended vaccines (13% LIC/LMIC, 28% UMIC, 44% HIC; p =0.007). Mixed-effects analyses showed significant differences in routine recommendations and full reimbursement by vaccine type and income group. The adjusted probability of routine recommendation was lower in LIC/LMIC than HIC countries (52.6% vs 77.6%; adjusted p=0.0013). Among recommended vaccines, more than 94% of influenza, pneumococcal, and hepatitis B vaccinations lacked full reimbursement in LIC/LMIC, based on adjusted estimates. Reimbursement gaps for HPV and herpes zoster vaccines remained substantial even in HIC. On-site vaccination was also less available in LIC/LMIC than in HIC (55% vs 78%; p=0.020). Conclusions Significant income-related disparities persist in vaccination policy and implementation for adults living with HIV. Gaps between recommendations and financial access are particularly pronounced in lower-income settings, while HPV and herpes zoster reimbursement remains limited across all income groups. Expanding HIV-specific vaccination policies, improving public reimbursement, and integrating vaccination into routine HIV services are essential to improve access to recommended vaccines for this population.

title: Association of vaginal microecological indicators with neutrophil extracellular trap markers in vaginal secretions across cervical lesion grades.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vaginal microenvironment disorder is related to cervical lesion development, and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) participate in tumour progression. Whether vaginal microecology indicators are associated with NET markers in vaginal secretions has not been examined. OBJECTIVE: To quantify the association between vaginal microecology indicators and vaginal secretion NET marker levels across cervical lesion grades. METHODS: Two hundred women formed control, cervicitis, low-grade and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion groups (n = 50, 50, 51, 49). Thirteen vaginal microecology indicators and HPV genotype were recorded. In 35 stratified vaginal secretion supernatants, myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA), citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3) and cell-free DNA (cfDNA) were measured. Spearman correlation and linear regression were applied. NET scores in GSE63514 and GSE7803 were derived by ssGSEA. RESULTS: Individual microecology indicators did not differ across groups after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. MPO-DNA and Cit-H3 were elevated in HPV-positive groups versus controls (P ≤ 0.003) without differing among lesion groups. Leukocyte esterase correlated with MPO-DNA (rho = 0.528, FDR = 0.037) and Cit-H3 (rho = 0.455, FDR = 0.049), and remained associated with MPO-DNA after adjustment for leukocyte grade (partial rho = 0.441, P = 0.009). In GSE63514, NET score increased with lesion grade (P = 0.003) and correlated with neutrophil infiltration (rho = 0.547, P < 0.001), which was not replicated in GSE7803 (trend P = 0.623). CONCLUSION: Vaginal inflammatory indicators, particularly leukocyte esterase, are positively associated with vaginal secretion MPO-DNA levels, reflecting local neutrophil-related inflammation rather than a mediating link in cervical lesion progression.

title: Self-reported health history from 70,724 individuals reveals novel HLA associations with allergy and other frequently underreported conditions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Variation in the HLA loci, located on human chromosome 6p, has been associated with hundreds of diseases and conditions. However, high levels of polymorphism that characterize the HLA system, coupled with generally modest effect sizes for most phenotypes, necessitate relatively large sample sizes to power association studies; meanwhile, high resolution HLA genotyping remains relatively resource intensive. These constraints limit identification of novel associations. While phenome-wide association studies (PheWAS) in the context of large registries with available electronic health records (EHR) have revealed new insights into the role of HLA in disease, many common health conditions are poorly represented in EHR due to the temporal nature of their occurrence or general underreporting. Further, these studies have generally been conducted with HLA genotyping data imputed from microarrays, rather than direct measurement of high-resolution genotypes. OBJECTIVE: To overcome these limitations and reveal novel HLA associations we undertook a PheWAS in many previously understudied health conditions. METHODS: We queried over 290 conditions, diseases and traits from 70,724 subjects registered with NMDP (formerly known as the National Marrow Donor Program) with available high-resolution HLA genotyping (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-DRB1, and HLA-DQB1). After stratifying according to self-reported geographic ancestry, we performed a logistic regression analysis adjusting for sex and age for HLA-phenotype association. RESULTS: We identified 48 significant HLA associations across self-reported geographic ancestry groups, confirming several known associations and uncovered fourteen novel associations. Most novel associations pertained to common infectious or allergic phenotypes that often go under-reported in the EHR. We identified a previously underappreciated yet very strong association between HLA-DRB1*04:01 and self-reported cefaclor adverse-reaction label of unverified mechanism (OR = 3.74, p-value 5.10E-28), which remained highly significant after excluding individuals reporting multiple drug hypersensitivities (OR = 3.13, p-value = 5.60E-15). Exploratory computational co-folding structure-and-affinity prediction identified a potential interaction between cefaclor and the P4 pocket of HLA-DRB1*04:01, providing a hypothesis-generating structural rationale that requires functional validation. If validated in independent cohorts with clinically characterized phenotypes and functional studies, this association may inform pharmacogenomic risk stratification and targeted prevention of adverse drug reactions. Other novel associations found, such as susceptibility to genital warts (HPV) and allergic rhinitis, reveal new insights into the role of specific HLA alleles in immune-mediated disease. Many of these novel associations were replicated in the independent All of Us cohort (AoU), while others showed the same trend for association, confirming the validity of this approach. CONCLUSION: Collectively, our findings demonstrate the value of integrating population-scale, high-resolution HLA genotypes with phenotyping beyond the EHR to reveal immunogenetic influences on common health outcomes. These findings motivate future functional studies and validation in clinically characterized cohorts to refine mechanistic understanding and determine potential clinical utility.

title: Epidemiological distribution of HPV genotypes and associated risk factors among HIV Positive and Negative women in Western Kenya
abstract: Abstract Background Human Papillomavirus infection is documented as the leading cause of cervical cancer globally. In Kenya, the burden of cervical cancer remains high despite cervical cancer preventions strategies. This study explores the epidemiological distribution and risk factors associated with HPV infection among HIV positive and negative women attending Gobei Health Center, Western Kenya. Methods We conducted a study between June and August 2024. A total of 308 eligible women aged 17–67 years who sought medical attention at Gobei Health Center and gave written consent were enrolled in the study. Each participant filled a structured questionnaire with the help of a research assistant where their socio-demographic, past reproductive history and sexual behavior characteristics were reported. Participants chose either HPV self-sampling or nurse-assisted cervical specimen collection approach. Riatol assay was used to determine HPV genotypes from each participant. Results The overall prevalence of HPV infection among women attending Gobei Health Centre was 37.6%. The most prevalent HPV genotype were HPV 52, 16, 18, 35, 31. HPV 16 was the most common genotype among HIV positive women. Being divorced was associated with HPV infection (AOR = 4.02, CI: 1.20–13.5, P = 0.024) and (AOR = 0.15, CI: 0.04–0.53 P = 0.003) respectively. There was a varied distribution of HPV viral load among HIV positive women compared to HIV negative women. Conclusion HPV infection remains common among HIV positive and Negative women attending Gobei Health Centre. Strengthening Cervical cancer prevention program such as comprehensive HPV vaccination and safe sex education in rural settings is important.

In Kenya, the burden of cervical cancer remains high despite cervical cancer preventions strategies. This study explores the epidemiological distribution and risk factors associated with HPV infection among HIV positive and negative women attending Gobei Health Center, Western Kenya. Methods We conducted a study between June and August 2024. A total of 308 eligible women aged 17–67 years who sought medical attention at Gobei Health Center and gave written consent were enrolled in the study. Each participant filled a structured questionnaire with the help of a research assistant where their socio-demographic, past reproductive history and sexual behavior characteristics were reported. Participants chose either HPV self-sampling or nurse-assisted cervical specimen collection approach. Riatol assay was used to determine HPV genotypes from each participant. Results The overall prevalence of HPV infection among women attending Gobei Health Centre was 37.6%. The most prevalent HPV genotype were HPV 52, 16, 18, 35, 31. HPV 16 was the most common genotype among HIV positive women. Being divorced was associated with HPV infection (AOR = 4.02, CI: 1.20–13.5, P = 0.024) and (AOR = 0.15, CI: 0.04–0.53 P = 0.003) respectively. There was a varied distribution of HPV viral load among HIV positive women compared to HIV negative women. Conclusion HPV infection remains common among HIV positive and Negative women attending Gobei Health Centre. Strengthening Cervical cancer prevention program such as comprehensive HPV vaccination and safe sex education in rural settings is important.

title: Cervical Neoplasia Among Canadian Armed Forces Regular Force Members, 2012-2024: A Descriptive Case Series.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cervical cancer is preventable through human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, routine screening, and timely follow up of abnormal results. However, limited evidence is available regarding cervical cancer burden and screening patterns and barriers within the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF). This study describes the demographic, military, clinical, and screening characteristics of cervical neoplasia cases diagnosed among CAF Regular Force members between 2012 and 2024. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective descriptive case series was conducted using electronic medical records from the Canadian Forces Health Information System. The International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes in the clinical extract were used to identify any cervical neoplasia diagnoses from January 1, 2012 to December 31, 2024. Incident cases were confirmed based on colposcopy‐directed biopsy results. Demographic and military-specific data at diagnosis were obtained from the Master Patient Index. Variables extracted from the health record included age at diagnosis, rank, screening history, HPV vaccination status, diagnostic pathways, stage at diagnosis, referral timelines, and follow-up outcomes. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize case characteristics and identify gaps in screening participation and follow-up adherence. RESULTS: A total of 23 incident cervical neoplasia cases were confirmed during the study period. The median age at diagnosis was 37 years (range: 24-52), and 47.8% were officers. 21.8% reported smoking at diagnosis. 43.5% of cases had missed (n = 7) or delayed (n = 3) at least 1 routine cervical cancer screening before diagnosis. 39.1% experienced delayed or missed follow-up after abnormal Pap results. Reported barriers to routine screening and follow-up included pandemic-related service interruptions, deployment or domestic posting, pregnancy, and childcare challenges. 39.1% (n = 9) had an abnormal result at the first recorded Pap test in the system. HPV vaccination completion was recorded for 52.2% of cases, and among those tested for HPV (n = 19), 31.6% were positive for types 16 or 18. Invasive cancer accounted for 56.5% of diagnoses, with 92.3% of invasive cases presenting at International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage I. Histology included squamous cell carcinoma (69.2%) and adenocarcinoma (30.8%). The median interval from abnormal screening result to diagnosis was 3.1 months (range: 0.7-61.9). No cervical cancer-related deaths were identified. CONCLUSION: This case series provides the first comprehensive description of cervical neoplasia among CAF Regular Force members over more than a decade. Findings highlight important opportunities to strengthen CAF prevention efforts, including improving screening participation and reducing delays in follow-up of abnormal tests. Enhanced reminder systems, reduced barriers to screening including self-testing, and targeted health promotion may reduce cervical cancer incidence and support the health and operational readiness of CAF personnel.

title: Changes in Post-Transplant Vaccine Coverage After Implementing Structured Vaccine Reviews in Pediatric Solid Organ Transplant Recipients in British Columbia, Canada: A Canadian Immunization Research Network Study.
abstract: Background Children with solid organ transplants (SOT) are at increased risk of infections but may be under-vaccinated. In 2021, our center implemented structured post-SOT vaccine reviews. We conducted a single-center, pre-post observational study with a repeated cross-sectional design to assess changes in vaccine coverage from 2020 to 2024. Methods We performed a chart review of SOT recipients aged 2-18 years who were ≥ 1 year post-transplant and followed at our clinic on March 1, 2020, and/or March 1, 2024. Patients eligible at both time points (repeat participants) were included in both cohorts; those eligible once (single-time-point participants) were included in the respective cohort. We assessed individual and overall vaccine coverage, defined as receipt of all recommended non-live, non-seasonal vaccines. Comparisons used the chi-square and paired McNemar's test (two-sided p Results Overall vaccine coverage increased from 33% in 2020 to 51% in 2024. The most prominent changes were observed for 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide (PPV23) and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines, with significant improvements among both single-time-point (PPV23: 58%-88%, p Conclusions Structured post-transplant vaccine reviews were associated with an increase in coverage across most vaccines and all organ subgroups, supporting its integration into routine post-transplant care and prospective, multicenter evaluation.

source_records.title: Changes in Post-Transplant Vaccine Coverage After Implementing Structured Vaccine Reviews in Pediatric Solid Organ Transplant Recipients in British Columbia, Canada: A Canadian Immunization Research Network Study.
source_records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Children with solid organ transplants (SOT) are at increased risk of infections but may be under-vaccinated. In 2021, our center implemented structured post-SOT vaccine reviews. We conducted a single-center, pre-post observational study with a repeated cross-sectional design to assess changes in vaccine coverage from 2020 to 2024. METHODS: We performed a chart review of SOT recipients aged 2-18 years who were ≥ 1 year post-transplant and followed at our clinic on March 1, 2020, and/or March 1, 2024. Patients eligible at both time points (repeat participants) were included in both cohorts; those eligible once (single-time-point participants) were included in the respective cohort. We assessed individual and overall vaccine coverage, defined as receipt of all recommended non-live, non-seasonal vaccines. Comparisons used the chi-square and paired McNemar's test (two-sided p < 0.05). RESULTS: Overall vaccine coverage increased from 33% in 2020 to 51% in 2024. Overall vaccine coverage among patients transplanted at age < 2 years was significantly lower compared to older children in 2020 but not in 2024. CONCLUSIONS: Structured post-transplant vaccine reviews were associated with an increase in coverage across most vaccines and all organ subgroups, supporting its integration into routine post-transplant care and prospective, multicenter evaluation.

title: Research progress on the immunoregulatory role of the female reproductive tract microbiota in HPV-associated cervical carcinogenesis and the oncogenic effects of microbial dysbiosis
abstract: Abstract Over the past several decades, the concept that human papillomavirus (HPV) can induce tumor formation has become well established. Persistent infection with high-risk HPV (hrHPV) types constitutes the primary risk factor for the development of nearly all cervical cancers, as well as a substantial proportion of malignant tumors of the vagina and vulva. The presence and abundance of certain bacterial species may confer protective effects against HPV infection and facilitate viral clearance, thereby reducing the risk of precancerous lesions in these anatomical sites. Conversely, other bacterial taxa may contribute to the promotion of pathological conditions. Consequently, elucidating the composition of the vaginal microbiota and its dysbiotic alterations in relation to HPV infection and persistence may enhance the predictive accuracy regarding infection outcomes. Furthermore, the precise identification of bacterial components associated with HPV-induced pathology holds potential clinical relevance and may inform alternative therapeutic strategies. Current technological advancements enable rapid, high-throughput analysis of the vaginal microbiome, which can be applied in longitudinal studies to delineate the roles of specific bacterial species in the initiation, prevention, progression, or regression of HPV-related cervical, vaginal, and vulvar lesions. Genetic and environmental factors that underlie the differential outcomes between viral clearance and cancer development remain an active area of investigation, with the microbiome emerging as a critical element that may modulate this balance by either promoting or inhibiting viral infection.

title: A Carboxyl-Coupled Light-Initiated Chemiluminescence Assay for HPV Bivalent Vaccine Potency
abstract: Background/Objectives: The development of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines is increasingly trending toward multivalency, and accurate quantification of HPV virus-like particles (VLPs) is critical for vaccine quality control. All marketed products currently rely on ELISA-based antigen quantification, which is complex and time-consuming. In accordance with the 3Rs principles, in vitro potency testing is expected to progressively replace in vivo testing. Therefore, efficient and convenient antigen quantification methods for multivalent HPV vaccines are essential to improve testing efficiency. Methods: In this study, photosensitive substances were loaded into beads of different diameters using a swelling method, and carboxyl groups were introduced onto the bead surfaces. By coupling HPV monoclonal antibodies via carboxyl groups, the use of high-risk coupling reagents was avoided, and a one-step light-initiated chemiluminescence assay (LiCA) was established for the in vitro relative potency testing of HPV vaccines. Results: The LiCA method established using 200 nm carboxyl-coupled beads for the HPV16/18 bivalent vaccine exhibited excellent linear range, specificity, accuracy, and precision. The LiCA results were comparable to those of ELISA; moreover, compared with ELISA, LiCA showed a lower detection limit and a wider dynamic range for both HPV16 and HPV18 VLP antigens, and was more convenient and time-saving to operate. Conclusions: A one-step LiCA was established using carboxyl-coupled beads with optimized diameters, providing an efficient and convenient approach for the in vitro relative potency testing of multivalent HPV vaccines based on large-particle VLP systems, which contributes to improved vaccine quality control and testing efficiency.

title: Understanding Cervical Screening Engagement Among Young South Asian Women: Perspectives of Women and Healthcare Professionals.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite increased uptake of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, cervical screening participation among younger South Asian women has declined, particularly in deprived areas in England. The reasons for this pattern remain poorly understood. This study explored barriers and facilitators to cervical screening among South Asian women aged 25-29 in a deprived locality. METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with South Asian women aged 25-29 (n = 15) and healthcare professionals involved in cervical screening delivery (n = 6) in Blackburn with Darwen. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Barriers to screening were multifactorial and included limited understanding of cervical screening and HPV, cultural norms surrounding modesty and sexuality, fear of community judgement and embarrassment, and structural challenges such as appointment access and competing responsibilities. Family networks acted as both barriers and facilitators. Healthcare professionals described adapting language to reduce fear, but highlighted service pressures related to staffing and funding, which constrained proactive engagement. Although most women reported receiving the HPV vaccination, understanding of HPV and the continued importance of cervical screening remained limited, highlighting opportunities to reinforce cervical screening education. CONCLUSION: Cervical screening engagement among young South Asian women is shaped by intersecting cultural, emotional, and structural influences, which may be intensified in deprived settings. HPV vaccination should be accompanied by clear communication about the continued importance of cervical screening, particularly where knowledge and awareness remain low. Culturally responsive communication, flexible service provision and community partnership approaches are needed to address persistent inequalities in screening uptake. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was informed by prior community engagement and public involvement work with underserved populations. Interview guides were developed in collaboration with a public advisor from the South Asian community to ensure they were relevant, inclusive, and reflective of community priorities.

METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with South Asian women aged 25-29 (n = 15) and healthcare professionals involved in cervical screening delivery (n = 6) in Blackburn with Darwen. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Barriers to screening were multifactorial and included limited understanding of cervical screening and HPV, cultural norms surrounding modesty and sexuality, fear of community judgement and embarrassment, and structural challenges such as appointment access and competing responsibilities. Family networks acted as both barriers and facilitators. Healthcare professionals described adapting language to reduce fear, but highlighted service pressures related to staffing and funding, which constrained proactive engagement. Although most women reported receiving the HPV vaccination, understanding of HPV and the continued importance of cervical screening remained limited, highlighting opportunities to reinforce cervical screening education. CONCLUSION: Cervical screening engagement among young South Asian women is shaped by intersecting cultural, emotional, and structural influences, which may be intensified in deprived settings. HPV vaccination should be accompanied by clear communication about the continued importance of cervical screening, particularly where knowledge and awareness remain low. Culturally responsive communication, flexible service provision and community partnership approaches are needed to address persistent inequalities in screening uptake. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was informed by prior community engagement and public involvement work with underserved populations. Interview guides were developed in collaboration with a public advisor from the South Asian community to ensure they were relevant, inclusive, and reflective of community priorities.

title: HPV vaccination uptake and schedule completion among adults aged 18-45 in Switzerland: a nationwide cross-sectional study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a highly effective strategy to prevent HPV-related diseases. Ensuring both sufficient coverage and appropriate dose timing is essential to reduce disease burden. While adolescent HPV vaccination coverage in Switzerland is routinely monitored, little is known about uptake and schedule completion among adults. Here, we assessed HPV vaccination uptake, dose timing, schedule completion as well as vaccination setting among adults in Switzerland. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional survey in 2023-2024 among adults aged 18-45 years. A total of 3847 participants submitted vaccination records and completed a questionnaire on vaccination setting. Vaccinations received during adolescence and adulthood were included. We assessed vaccination uptake (receipt of ≥1 dose), dose timing and completion of schedules according to age and dosing-interval criteria. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between schedule completion and age group, gender, region and vaccination setting. RESULTS: Overall, 42.8% of females and 12.2% of males received ≥1 HPV vaccine dose, with the highest uptake among women aged 18-26 years (80.4%). Among vaccinated participants, 72.7% met the criteria for a complete schedule. Among two-dose recipients, 29.0% received their second dose less than 5 months after the first, a shorter interval than recommended for a two-dose schedule. Compared with vaccination across multiple settings, vaccination exclusively through school-based programmes or paediatricians was associated with higher adjusted odds of schedule completion (adjusted OR (aOR) 2.27, 95% CI 1.21 to 4.27, and aOR 2.40, 95% CI 1.28 to 4.51, respectively). CONCLUSION: HPV vaccination uptake among adults in Switzerland remains modest, particularly among men. Although most vaccinated participants met the criteria for a complete schedule, short dosing intervals were common among two-dose recipients. Increasing uptake, clearer guidance on age-specific dosing requirements and increasing follow-up may help to improve coverage.

title: Cancer-specific T cell receptor discovery using 150,000 clinical genomics samples.
abstract: T cell receptors (TCRs) can enable detection and elimination of cancer cells via recognition of cancer-specific peptides presented on human leukocyte antigen (HLA). We speculated that shared cancer antigens could be recognized by recurrent ("public") TCRs, which might be identifiable using statistical methods. Here, we identified public TCRs against therapeutically relevant targets via computational analysis of large-scale bulk RNA sequencing data obtained from routine clinical genomics testing. Using data from ∼150,000 patient tumor samples, we identified TCR chains that were associated with well-known cancer antigens, including human papillomavirus, mutated KRAS, and CT83. We devised methods for pairing enriched TCR-α and TCR-β chain sequences and validated 44 TCRs across nine peptide-HLA targets for antigen recognition, including potent cytotoxic TCRs. Our results suggest that public anticancer TCRs are common and may represent a new source for the development of cancer therapeutics.

title: Evaluation of the Clinical Utility of Circulating Tumor DNA in the Management of Patients With Nonmetastatic Head and Neck Cancer: Protocol for a Prospective Bicentric Study (CIRVAD).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative head and neck cancers, often linked to tobacco and alcohol exposure, have a poor prognosis and high recurrence rates. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is a promising biomarker for detecting minimal residual disease and monitoring treatment response. Recent studies show that ctDNA can detect recurrence earlier than clinical or radiological methods. Prospective trials are needed to validate its clinical utility. OBJECTIVE: The primary objective is to assess postoperative ctDNA as a predictor of 28-month progression-free survival. Secondary objectives include evaluating ctDNA levels before and after treatment as predictors of recurrence, studying ctDNA dynamics during follow-up in relation to survival, and exploring their association with tumor characteristics and surgical outcomes. METHODS: This prospective, bicentric study evaluates ctDNA in patients undergoing surgery for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Plasma ctDNA concentrations will be measured quantitatively in ng/mL before and 1 to 2 weeks after surgery, with or without adjuvant radiotherapy or chemotherapy. Progression-free survival is defined as the time from surgery to disease progression or death, and recurrence-free survival as the time to clinically confirmed recurrence. Overall and disease-specific survival will also be assessed. Changes in ctDNA levels over follow-up and clinical characteristics will be compared between patients with and without progression at 28 months. Absolute and relative variations in ctDNA preoperatively and postoperatively will be described, and surgical quality will be evaluated according to resection margins (R0, R1, R2). RESULTS: As of August 2026, study preparation, including protocol development and methodological validation, has been completed. The study is currently entering the implementation phase, with regulatory procedures, funding applications, and site initiation activities underway. No participants have been recruited at the time of manuscript submission, as recruitment has not yet begun. Recruitment is expected to start following regulatory approval and funding acquisition. The funding status remains pending as of August 2026, with funding applications underway. Participant recruitment and data collection are projected to take approximately 24 months, followed by a 28-month follow-up period. Data analysis has not yet started and will be conducted after completion of the follow-up period. The first study results are therefore expected to become available after the completion of data collection and follow-up, although a precise publication timeline (season/year) cannot yet be determined. CONCLUSIONS: This study aims to provide key data on the potential of ctDNA to detect early recurrence in HPV-negative cancers and could inform personalized patient monitoring and management.

title: The Effect of Perceived Spokesperson Masculinity on HPV Vaccination Intention among College Students
abstract: Abstract The human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is a highly effective preventive measure against cervical cancer, genital warts, and other infectious diseases that affect both men and women. Because the vaccine was initially recommended for girls/women, a gap in vaccine uptake between women and men persists. Guided by the model of source credibility and protection motivation theory, this study examined whether perceived spokesperson masculinity may potentially “defeminize” the perceived HPV stigma and increase college students’ HPV vaccination intention. The study adopted a 2\(\:\times\:\)2 between-subjects design ( N = 267) comparing unvaccinated U.S. college students’ responses to a more muscular vs. less muscular fictional male physician with an older- vs. a younger appearance. Findings showed that participants perceived the physician who appeared more muscular and older-looking as more agentic-masculine, which, in turn, increased their perceived credibility. This credibility perception led to higher vaccination intention, but it did not directly influence beliefs about the HPV threats and the vaccine’s efficacy. Two mediation paths were statistically significant: from physician’s agentic masculinity via physician credibility and coping efficacy, respectively, to vaccination intention. Both threat and coping efficacy perception were also found to be positively related to vaccination intention. This study extends our understanding of how perceived credibility of spokespersons in vaccine communication may facilitate beneficial HPV-threat evaluation and increase protective action intention.

title: Program-level evaluation of population-based HPV screening in Van, Türkiye: screening activity, test positivity, genotype distribution and follow-up data capture in a retrospective record-based study
abstract: Abstract Background Province-level evidence on the implementation of population-based HPV screening in eastern Türkiye remains limited. This study aimed to describe screening activity relative to the programme-defined target population, HPV test positivity, recorded genotype patterns, histopathological diagnoses, and available follow-up information within the cervical cancer screening programme in Van Province. Methods This retrospective, record-based programme evaluation used aggregated programme data from 2022 through the first two months of 2026 and individual-level records for HPV-positive women from 2023–2025. Annual screening activity ratios were calculated using programme-defined target populations. Age and recorded genotype distributions were described among HPV-positive women. Histopathological diagnoses and referral-related information were reported as available programme records because individual-level linkage and complete pathway denominators were unavailable. Temporal change in programme HPV test positivity was assessed using the Cochran-Armitage trend test. Results Across the study periods, annual screening counts summed to 94,123 records, with 2,078 HPV-positive results (2.21%). The screening activity ratio increased from 17.1% in 2022 to 95.5% in 2024 and decreased to 67.9% in 2025. Observed programme HPV test positivity declined from 3.17% in 2022 to 1.80% in 2025 (p for trend < 0.001). Among 1,810 HPV-positive women with individual-level data, the mean age was 44.5 years. HPV16 was the most frequently recorded specific genotype (36.4%), HPV16 and/or HPV18 was recorded in 43.8%, and at least one recorded oncogenic genotype targeted by the nine-valent vaccine was identified in 55.4%. Multiple specifically identified HPV genotypes were recorded in 16.5%. Programme records contained 394 histopathological diagnoses during 2023–2025, including three invasive cervical cancer records. Available follow-up data did not permit calculation of referral, hospital attendance, colposcopy, biopsy, or treatment completion rates. Conclusions HPV screening activity in Van varied substantially across years, while observed programme test positivity declined during 2022–2025; this decline should not be interpreted as evidence of reduced population HPV prevalence. Recorded genotype findings were dominated by HPV16, but variation in type-specific reporting limits temporal interpretation. Improved standardization of genotype reporting and individual-level linkage across screening, referral, diagnosis, histopathology, and treatment would strengthen programme monitoring.

title: Cervical cancer on-site mass-screening device utilizing multiple biomarkers in Swab samples for surveillance in the resource limited areas of India
abstract: At the World Health Assembly in August 2020, a target was set to eradicate cervical cancer globally by 2030 (incidence < 4/100,000) with 90% vaccination coverage, 70% screening coverage, and 90% treatment coverage. India has a worrying prevalence of between 6 and 30 percent, due to HPV infections and low awareness in rural areas. HPV infections and cervical cancer disease development window period is anytime between 6 and 20 years. Thus mass screening of the population will play a very crucial role. KayaCervi, a lab-free, point-of-care mass screening device based on fluorescence EEM technology, consisting of a cartridge, a reader and a microchip was clinically validated in the study. Initially, ten biomarkers were compared using ELISA and Pap smear. Four (p16INK4a, Ki 67, HPV16, HPV18) were selected. Swab validation was performed with cohorts’ of 200 hospital patients and 800 healthy community females, benchmarked against LBC to optimize sensitivity and ensure high specificity. The community-based validation study was to evaluate the performance of the device as a mass-screening tool among apparently healthy women. In such settings, the majority of participants are disease-negative, and high specificity is essential to minimize false-positive results, unnecessary referrals, psychological distress, and healthcare costs. Sensitivity was measured during the standardization phase by screening participants and confirmed positive cases. Initial findings used biomarkers p16NK4A, Ki67, HPV16, and HPV18 to categorize women into high, moderate, and low risk. The design of the cartridge ensured efficient sample capture and quantification, integrating mechanisms to correct for various light wavelengths during analysis. In community-based evaluation (N = 801), the device demonstrated an overall agreement of 98.0% with the reference standard. Cohen's kappa coefficient was 0.545, indicating moderate agreement beyond chance. The device achieved 100% sensitivity, 98.0% specificity, 38.5% positive predictive value, 100% negative predictive value, and 98.0% overall accuracy and identified high percentage of infections in the apparently healthy women comparable to the liquid based cytology reading done for the relative cellular changes. This study validated KayaCervi, a portable, laboratory-independent point-of-care diagnostic device developed to address India's high burden of cervical cancer. The device integrates a fluorescence-based detection platform with a four-target biomarker panel comprising p16INK4a, Ki-67, HPV16, and HPV18, achieving a specificity of 86–90% in community-based rural screening. As a rapid, low-cost, and user-friendly screening tool, KayaCervi has the potential to democratize access to cervical cancer screening by overcoming barriers related to laboratory infrastructure, trained personnel, and patient follow-up. Further, it include the need for larger, prospective, multicenter studies involving geographically diverse populations, with the biomarker panel and diagnostic thresholds predefined before evaluation and with an appropriate independently established reference standard. Such studies will be essential to confirm the reproducibility, generalizability, diagnostic performance, clinical utility and implementation feasibility of KayaCervi before large-scale deployment. Its suitability for decentralized, large-scale population screening is particularly important given the prolonged natural history of cervical carcinogenesis, where persistent HPV infection may take 15–20 years to progress to invasive cancer, providing a critical window for early detection and timely intervention. This highlights the public health significance by emphasizing the long preclinical phase and the opportunity for early intervention.

title: Comparative Evaluation of AI Chatbots for Medical Research: Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
abstract: Abstract Background The use of generative AI in research and clinical practice is rapidly expanding, offering unprecedented capabilities in pattern extraction and data analysis. However, its application raises critical concerns regarding the accuracy and reliability of the information provided. Objective The aim of this study is to analyze and compare the performance of 4 generative AI platforms (ChatGPT, Grok, Meta AI, and Perplexity) in retrieving bibliographic references within the medical and health care field and to assess factual accuracy and information retrieval strategies. Methods A cross-sectional observational study was conducted based on the simulation of 3 bibliographic queries with varying levels of specificity (aflatoxin toxicity, hospital sanitization, and human papillomavirus vaccination). Each prompt was administered in triple iteration on each platform operating in “Guest” mode. Factual accuracy was verified through a manual cross-check against the Scopus and Google Scholar databases using a hierarchical query strategy prioritized by DOI. The incidence of hallucinations was quantified via a standardized scoring system (range 0‐5) based on metadata correctness. Categorical associations were analyzed using the Pearson chi-square test, while nonparametric continuous variables (hallucination score, publication year, and citation count) were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test. Results Of the 360 requested references, 273 were generated (task completion rate: 75.8%). Among these, 190 adhered to the requested article format (instruction adherence rate: 69.6% of generated outputs). Fact-checking revealed that 128 of these 190 validly formatted articles (metadata accuracy rate: 67.4%) showed an exact match with real evidence, resulting in an overall strict yield of 35.6% (128/360) from the initial requested references. The ability to provide real references depended significantly on the AI model used (χ 6 2=192.5; P <.001). Kruskal-Wallis tests revealed statistically significant differences among the models across all analyzed dimensions ( P <.001). Grok emerged as the most reliable model, achieving 71 out of 90 (78.9%) exact matches, exhibiting minimal hallucinations (mean score 0.2, SD 0.5), and showing a marked propensity toward recent sources (median year 2022, IQR 2019.0-2024.8). ChatGPT demonstrated robust stability, with 46 out of 90 (51.1%) exact matches, and anchored itself to older (median year 2020, IQR 2011.0-2023.0), highly cited literature (median 73.5, IQR 10.8‐718.0 citations). Perplexity exhibited critical rates of total hallucination and a structural inability to distinguish scientific articles from gray literature. Meta AI systematically failed the task, producing entirely incorrect data on a single occasion (0/10, 0% exact matches). Conclusions Under the specific testing conditions of this study, the evaluated large language models demonstrated a lack of the necessary reliability to replace validated bibliographic databases, primarily due to response instability and a high incidence of metadata fabrication. The results highlight the urgency of introducing structured AI literacy programs across medical education, promoting the use of such technologies exclusively as a complementary tool and always subject to rigorous human fact-checking.

title: Undertreatment of Cervical Precancer Among Screen-Positive Women Living with HIV in Kenya
abstract: PURPOSE Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality among women living with HIV (WLWH) in sub-Saharan Africa. Although screening coverage has improved, evidence on completion of post-screening diagnostic evaluation and treatment remains limited. We described screening results and the post-screening management cascade among WLWH receiving HIV care in Nairobi, Kenya. METHODS We analyzed Project CN001 data from the National Cancer Institute-funded CASCADE Clinical Trials Network at the Coptic Hope Center for Infectious Diseases in Nairobi. We included WLWH aged 25-49 years who underwent visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) and/or high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing between March 11, 2025, and January 16, 2026, with at least 1 month of follow-up. VIA-positive women with fully visualized transformation zones (TZ) were eligible for same-day thermal ablation; those with non-fully visualized TZ or suspicious findings were referred for colposcopy. hrHPV-positive women were recommended for VIA triage. RESULTS Among 988 WLWH screened with VIA (n = 857) and/or hrHPV testing (n = 136), median age was 41 years (IQR, 35-46), and median time since HIV diagnosis was 10.5 years (IQR, 5-16). Among VIA-screened women, 63 (7.4%) had VIA-positive or suspicious findings and 794 (92.6%) were VIA-negative. TZ distribution varied by age, with younger women more likely to have TZ1 and older women more likely to have TZ3. Among 63 women with VIA-positive or suspicious findings, 37 (58.7%) received same-day thermal ablation and 26 (41.3%) were referred for colposcopy. Only 4 referred women (15.4%) underwent colposcopy: CIN3 was detected in 1, CIN2 in 1, and no CIN in 2. The woman with CIN2 received LEEP/LLETZ 9 days after; the woman with CIN3 and the remaining 24 referred women received no treatment (96.2%). Among 136 women undergoing hrHPV testing, 31 (22.8%) were hrHPV-positive; only 5 (16.1%) underwent VIA triage, and all were VIA-negative. CONCLUSION Among WLWH engaged in HIV care in Kenya, screening uptake was high and same-day ablation was feasible. However, screen-positive women referred for further evaluation rarely completed it and often received no treatment. Reducing financial and logistical barriers and strengthening pragmatic screen-and-treat pathways are essential to improve cervical cancer prevention among WLWH.

title: Replacing an HPV DNA assay with an HPV E6/E7 mRNA full-genotype kit before ART is associated with shorter time to oocyte retrieval without evidence of a lower clinical pregnancy rate: a real-world before–after cohort study
abstract: Introduction Cervical HPV assessment before assisted reproductive technology (ART) can lead to additional evaluation and delay subsequent treatment. We compared treatment timing and pregnancy outcomes before and after replacement of HPV DNA testing with HPV E6/E7 mRNA full-genotype testing. Methods This single-centre retrospective before–after cohort study included 4,740 women undergoing ART between 1 May 2024 and 31 May 2026. Time to treatment readiness (TTR) was defined as the interval from HPV reporting to subsequent oocyte retrieval within the index ART cycle. The TTR-evaluable cohort included 3,543 women (DNA, n = 3,037; mRNA, n = 506). Between-era differences in TTR were assessed using non-parametric methods and median quantile regression. Clinical pregnancy was evaluated in a nested cohort of 942 women (DNA, n = 732; mRNA, n = 210) using a margin-based safety assessment and logistic regression. Results Median TTR was 30.5 days (IQR 21.0–58.5) in the HPV E6/E7 mRNA era and 63.0 days (IQR 30.0–152.0) in the HPV DNA era ( P < 0.001). The Hodges–Lehmann location-shift estimate was −26.0 days (95% CI −31.0 to −22.0). After adjustment for female age, male age, body mass index (BMI), anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), and ART cycle status, median TTR was 30.15 days shorter in the HPV E6/E7 mRNA era (95% CI −34.74 to −25.56; P < 0.001). TTR ≥30 days occurred in 53.4% and 75.8% of women, respectively (OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.30–0.44; P < 0.001). Clinical pregnancy occurred in 59.0% of women in the HPV E6/E7 mRNA era and 46.6% in the HPV DNA era. The risk difference was 12.46 percentage points (95% CI 4.89–20.03), and the lower confidence limit exceeded the −5-percentage-point safety margin. The adjusted OR for clinical pregnancy was 1.85 (95% CI 1.33–2.56; P < 0.001). Conclusions HPV E6/E7 mRNA full-genotype testing was associated with a shorter interval to oocyte retrieval than HPV DNA testing. Among pregnancy-evaluable women, the clinical pregnancy rate met the prespecified supportive non-inferiority criterion, with the lower 95% confidence limit for the between-era risk difference exceeding the −5-percentage-point margin.

title: Knowledge and Awareness of Cervical Cancer Prevention and HPV Vaccination among Medical and Nursing Students in Selective Tertiary Care Hospitals
abstract: Background: Cervical cancer is a significant public health challenge, particularly in low-income countries. Prevention, including Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and routine screening, is vital in reducing its burden. Medical and nursing students and future healthcare providers must assess awareness and prevention strategies. This study assessed the level of knowledge and awareness about cervical cancer and its prevention among medical and nursing students. Materials and methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 70 medical students of Marine City Medical College and Institute of Applied Health Sciences and 94 nursing students of Marine City Nursing College and Anwara Noor Nursing College of Chattogram using a questionnaire to assess their knowledge of cervical cancer, its prevention and the importance of HPV vaccination. Data were analyzed to evaluate the overall awareness level and identify gaps in knowledge. Results: This study of 70 medical and 94 nursing students found higher overall awareness of cervical cancer and the HPV vaccine among nursing students. While most recognized cervical cancer as common and preventable, knowledge of risk factors and preventive methods like Pap smear and vaccination was limited. Awareness was greater among city-schooled students and social media was the main information source. Only a small percentage had received the HPV vaccine (8% medical, 18.4% nursing). Conclusions: This study highlights significant knowledge gaps, underscoring the need for regular assessments and targeted educational interventions. Enhancing awareness among healthcare trainees and greater involvement of family physicians are essential for improving HPV vaccine acceptance and public education. IAHS Medical Journal Vol 9(1), June 2026; 44-50

This study assessed the level of knowledge and awareness about cervical cancer and its prevention among medical and nursing students. Materials and methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 70 medical students of Marine City Medical College and Institute of Applied Health Sciences and 94 nursing students of Marine City Nursing College and Anwara Noor Nursing College of Chattogram using a questionnaire to assess their knowledge of cervical cancer, its prevention and the importance of HPV vaccination. title: Data-Driven age structured model for optimal control and cost-effective HPV vaccine uptake for cervical cancer reduction in Tanzania
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the leading sexually transmitted infection worldwide and the primary cause of cervical cancer, a major cause of mortality among women in sub-Saharan Africa. In Tanzania, where HPV poses a significant health burden, effective vaccination strategies are critical. We develop an age-structured PDE model capturing HPV transmission in both sexes and cervical cancer progression in females. The model, consisting of ten coupled PDEs, was calibrated using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods with Tanzanian HPV incidence data (2018–2023), confirming reliable parameter estimates. Applying the Lotka Sharpe McKendrick integral approach, we derived the effective reproduction number R ( ω ) dependent on age-specific vaccination rate. We proved local and global stability of the disease-free equilibrium when R ( ω ) < 1 , supported by numerical simulations showing infection decline under this condition. We formulated an optimization framework balancing epidemiological impact and vaccination costs, identifying age groups that maximize cost-effectiveness. Simulations revealed that extending vaccination beyond ages 9–14, to include 14–29 year old, substantially reduces infections and cervical cancer incidence, with a critical age threshold a ∗ = 26 indicating that a single cohort strategy is optimal. Increased vaccination intensity notably benefits women aged 20–30, where infection peaks. Finally, we strongly recommend sustaining adolescent vaccination programs and implementing targeted catch-up campaigns up to age 29. Expanding and maintaining HPV vaccination programs is an effective, feasible, and cost-efficient strategy to protect girls and young women from cervical cancer, the leading HPV-related disease in Tanzania and to accelerate progress toward the WHO cervical cancer elimination goals.

title: Vulvar High-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion in Primary Lymphedema With Severe Genital Lymphorrhea: A Case Report.
abstract: Vulvar high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) is an HPV-associated premalignant lesion requiring prompt management. Its occurrence in primary lymphedema is rarely described. We report a 37-year-old woman with childhood-onset primary lymphedema who presented after 31 years of clinical quiescence with recurrent right lower-extremity and genital lymphedema presenting with vulvar swelling, erythema, follicular lesions, and persistent lymphorrhea. Indocyanine green (ICG) lymphography confirmed recurrent combined genital and lower-extremity lymphedema. Lymphaticovenular anastomosis (LVA) and abnormal perineal tissue excision were performed during the same operative session at different sites. Histopathology unexpectedly demonstrated multifocal vulvar HSIL with lymphangiectatic change. Immunohistochemistry showed p16 and Ki-67 overexpression, wild-type p53, D2-40 positivity, and CD34 negativity. HPV genotyping detected HPV16 and HPV42. Lymphorrhea decreased substantially, and leg volume decreased by 9.5%. Chronic genital lymphedema can obscure premalignant disease; morphologically abnormal or persistent vulvar lesions warrant histopathological assessment. LVA may reduce lymphorrhea and edema but cannot replace definitive oncologic treatment.

title: Multi-platform social media use and trust, health beliefs, and HPV vaccination willingness among Chinese university students
abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage among Chinese university students remains low despite effective vaccines and national elimination targets. How multi-channel social media shapes vaccination decisions in China's digital environment is not well understood. This study investigated determinants of HPV vaccination willingness among university students using the Health Belief Model (HBM), focusing on media exposure, trust, and gender-specific barriers. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 250 university students in Guangdong, China. The survey measured sociodemographic factors, HPV knowledge, HBM constructs (perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, barriers), perceived vaccine safety, browsing and active search frequency on five social media platforms, trust in different information sources, and vaccination willingness. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors. Gender-stratified analyses examined specific barriers. Results Of the 250 students, 78.0% (195/250) expressed willingness to get the HPV vaccine. Greater HPV vaccination willingness was associated with being female (aOR = 10.24, 95% CI: 4.05–25.92), age 18-26 years (aOR = 4.83, 95% CI: 1.41–16.50), higher HPV knowledge (aOR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.03–1.35), greater perceived vaccine safety (aOR = 4.50, 95% CI: 2.01–10.09), greater perceived susceptibility (aOR = 4.48, 95% CI: 2.08–9.64), and greater social media trust (aOR = 2.12, 95% CI: 1.20–3.75). Passive browsing and active information searching were not retained in the final multivariable model. Social media platforms (WeChat, Xiaohongshu, Weibo) were the most frequently used information channels but received the lowest trust ratings; healthcare providers were trusted most. Willing students reported higher browsing frequencies on WeChat, Xiaohongshu, and Weibo than unwilling students ( p < 0.05), but these differences did not persist in the multivariate model. Male and female students had different barrier profiles: infertility myths were more common among males (14.7 vs. 4.5%, p < 0.001); worry about menstrual changes was reported by 20.0% of males and 27.7% of females ( p = 0.094). Conclusions Social media was frequently used but received lower average trust than healthcare providers; social media use frequency was not independently associated with willingness. Instead of just putting more content on social media, efforts should focus on building knowledge, using trusted sources such as healthcare providers, and on correcting gender-specific misunderstandings.

title: 509 QUILT-3.100: phase 1 open-label study to evaluate safety and determine the maximum tolerated dose of iBRX-042 in participants with hpv-associated head and neck tumors
abstract: Background Infection with human papilloma virus (HPV) confers a risk of subsequent malignancy. While prophylactic vaccines against HPV are available, there is a need for a therapeutic vaccine that effectively treats HPV-associated cancers. IBRX-042 is a recombinant non-replicating human adenovirus serotype 5 (hAd5) vector modified by removal of early 1 (E1), E2b, and E3 gene regions and insertion of non-oncogenic regions E6 and E7. Importantly, the hAd5 recombinant vector replicates episomally without genome insertion and integration, while maintaining independent antigen production.Methods QUILT-3.100 ( NCT05976828) is a phase 1, open-label study evaluating the safety and maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of IBRX-042 in participants with HPV-associated solid tumors. Two dose levels were tested: Cohort (C) 1 received 1e11 virus particles (VP)/dose (n = 3); C2 received 5e11 VP/dose (n = 7). Primary endpoint was MTD, secondary endpoints included safety, serum antibody titers, and peripheral blood T-cell responses. Key inclusion criteria included participants with histologically confirmed HPV- or p16-positive carcinoma who have received at least one standard of care therapy per NCCN guidelines. IBRX-042 was administrated via subcutaneous injection at weeks 1, 4, and 7.Results The safety population enrolled 10 participants with HPV-positive solid tumors; nine participants had a head and neck tumor, including tongue, tonsils, and tonsils + lymph nodes. The median age was 65.5 years and 80% were male. Seventy percent of participants had baseline Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0; 30% had ECOG of 1. In exploratory analysis, HPV-specific T-cell immune responses were observed in participant samples; data collection is ongoing. All participants experienced at least one treatment-related adverse event (TRAE); all grade 1 or 2. TRAEs generally included administration site reactions (pain, erythema, swelling) and myalgia. Serious adverse events (SAEs) were observed in 30% of participants: one participant in C1 experienced disease progression; two participants in C2 experienced overlapping SAEs including hemoptysis, pleural effusion, respiratory failure, atrial fibrillation, and/or hypertension. All SAEs were considered unrelated. No dose limiting toxicities (DLTs) were observed. MTD was determined to be 5e11 VP/dose. At the time of this report, 4/5 participants were alive and the one that expired was in C1.Conclusions The QUILT-3.100 trial determined the MTD (5e11 VP/dose) for IBRX-042 in participants with HPV-associated solid tumors, including head and neck. The safety profile for this HPV-directed cancer vaccine was well tolerated with no DLTs. Future clinical studies in combination with other immune-activating therapies are planned.

title: RPS17 can act as a tumor suppressive ribosomal protein in human cell lines.
abstract: Certain ribosomal proteins (RPs) function as tumor suppressors. For example, RPL5 and RPL11 suppress oncogenesis by binding to MDM2 and thereby up-regulating p53, a mechanism referred to as the RP-MDM2-p53 cascade. However, whether other cancer-associated ribosomal proteins actually function as tumor suppressors has remained largely unclear. Previously, we showed that siRNA-mediated silencing of RPS17, in combination with expression of HPV16 E7 and activated KRAS G12V, transformed normal human fibroblasts. Here, we expanded our study to perform a functional analysis of RPS17 as a tumor suppressor. We first demonstrate that shRNA-mediated RPS17 silencing also promotes oncogenic transformation of human fibroblasts in vitro and in vivo. Conversely, its overexpression inhibits the soft agar colony formation of colon cancer-derived HCT116 cells in a p53-dependent manner. RPS17 weakly interacts with MDM2. However, unlike RPL5 and RPL11, overexpression of RPS17 does not increase p53 levels and its silencing induces p53, suggesting that the RP-MDM2-p53 cascade might not be a major pathway for its tumor-suppressive function. We further show that RPS17 binds to nucleophosmin and modulates its nuclear localization. Although the detailed molecular mechanisms underlying the tumor-suppressive function of RPS17 remain to be elucidated, this study provides evidence that RPS17 can function as a tumor suppressor.

title: The Digital Twin Paradigm in Head and Neck Cancer: Clinical Opportunities and Challenges.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) represents a significant public health challenge. Its treatment is characterized by high anatomical complexity and a critical need for functional preservation of speech, swallowing, and respiration. While multimodality care, including surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy, has substantially improved patient survival, there are still high rates of life-altering toxicities and low response rates to immunotherapy. Current clinical decision-making largely relies on "digital snapshots"-static representations derived from population-based statistics and time point-specific imaging-which usually fail to account for the rapid anatomical and biological change during the course of treatment. Digital twins hold great promise in accelerating scientific breakthroughs and transforming oncology treatment and precision medicine through the creation of high-fidelity virtual patient representations that integrate real-time biological, anatomical, and clinical data. In this viewpoint, we propose 3 interconnected digital twins to establish a conceptual framework for the HNSCC digital twin. These digital twins include the anatomical twin, using virtual surgical planning and augmented reality for geometric precision; the dosimetric twin, using daily imaging and synthetic computed tomography generation for automated adaptive radiotherapy; and the biological twin, integrating deep phenotyping, radiomics, and mechanistic omics to simulate individualized therapeutic trajectories. Beyond acute care, we explore the clinical utility of digital twins in navigating the "de-escalation dilemma" for human papillomavirus-associated disease and improving survivorship through digital phenotyping. With the advent of longitudinal data from medical-grade Internet-of-Things sensors and circulating tumor DNA kinetics, digital twins can serve as active sentinels, detecting functional decline or subclinical events months before clinical manifestation. Furthermore, the implementation of synthetic control arms via virtual populations offers an avenue to accelerate clinical trials and address ethical issues in rare molecular subtypes. Despite this potential, substantial barriers to implementation remain, including profound anatomical instability during treatment, the "black box" nature of deep learning algorithms, and the challenges of multiscale data integration. We provide a technical roadmap for the development of "morphing" digital twins-dynamic systems capable of continuous geometric and biological auditing. By bridging the gap between the macroscopic world of radiation physics and the microscopic world of cellular evolution, digital twins may help shift the management of HNSCC from population-based statistical probability toward more individualized, biologically informed decision-making, with the goal of optimizing HNSCC management while preserving essential patient functions.

title: Viral Infection Across the Kidney Transplant Continuum: Screening, Prevention, Management, and Oncogenesis
abstract: Viral infections influence every stage of the kidney transplantation continuum, shaping immunologic risk, graft outcomes, and long term patient survival. Pre transplant serologic assessments guide critical decisions, including vaccinations, the avoidance of lymphocyte depleting induction in Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) mismatched candidates and the selection of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) prophylaxis tailored to donor–recipient serostatus. Acceptance of hepatitis C viremic donor organs has significantly reduced wait times, while human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) positive donor organs remain restricted to HIV positive recipients. Post transplant, viral pathogens are major drivers of morbidity: CMV functions as an immunomodulator that increases susceptibility to rejection and opportunistic fungal infections, and routine surveillance for CMV and BK viremia is essential, especially following rejection therapies. BK virus nephropathy, adenovirus nephropathy, and JC virus nephropathy can lead to progressive allograft dysfunction. Additionally, COVID 19 and parvovirus infections have been associated with collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) and severe graft injury. Persistent viral infections and virus associated glomerulopathies contribute to chronic graft loss, while EBV driven post transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD) remains a significant cause of cancer related mortality. Transplant recipients are also at increased risk for persistent human papillomavirus infection (HPV) and progression to anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies. Finally, donor derived viral infections, including rabies, West Nile virus (WNV), and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV), though rare, are well described in the literature. Collectively, these viral complications substantially impact morbidity, graft survival, and overall mortality in kidney transplant recipients.

title: Mapping Fear and Hope in HPV Vaccine Communication on Sina Weibo: Topic Modeling and Content Analysis
abstract: HPV vaccines became available in mainland China in 2016, yet concerns surrounding HPV vaccination have continued to feature prominently in public discourse. Against this background, this study examined how HPV and HPV vaccination are discussed on Sina Weibo and how threat- and efficacy-related message components are represented within this discourse. Drawing on the Extended Parallel Process Model (EPPM), this study analyzed 219,068 posts on Sina Weibo published between 2018 and 2024 using topic modeling and theory-guided content analysis. Topic modeling revealed a substantial increase in HPV-related discussions over the study period and identified five prominent themes: health behaviors, HPV vaccination, cervical cancer prevention, nine-valent HPV vaccine appointment scheduling, and HPV infection. Content analysis further revealed an imbalance between threat and efficacy components in fear-appeal messages. Efficacy information occurred more frequently than threat information, with self-efficacy appearing most frequently, followed by response efficacy, susceptibility, and severity. Spearman correlation analyses showed that severity and self-efficacy were positively associated with the number of user forwards, whereas susceptibility and response efficacy were not significantly associated with forwarding activity in the reported analysis. These findings extend the application of the EPPM to naturally occurring social media communication by demonstrating how threat and efficacy components are unevenly represented and differently associated with observable user engagement. The study also highlights the importance of designing HPV communication that balances information about health threats with clear and actionable efficacy information.
