title: Clinical Dental Guidelines for Patients with Head and Neck Cancer Treated with Radiotherapy: A Scoping Review
abstract: Head and neck cancer (HNC) remains a major global health concern, currently ranking as the seventh most common malignancy worldwide. Accounting for roughly 660,000 new cases and 325,000 deaths each year, the global burden of the disease is expected to grow by 30% by 2030. Squamous cell carcinomas (SCC) make up approximately 90% of all HNC cases, primarily originating from the mucosal lining of the oral cavity, pharynx, and larynx. Major risk factors for HNC include smoking, alcohol consumption, and infection with oncogenic viruses, such as human papillomavirus (HPV) for oropharyngeal cancer (HPVOC), and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) for nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC). HNCs are exhibiting a gradual decline in global incidence, partly attributable to the reduced consumption of tobacco. In contrast, the occurrence of HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer, primarily caused by HPV type 16, is rising, particularly among younger populations in North America and northern Europe. This upward trend is linked to greater clinical awareness, improved recognition of the relationship between HPV and HNCs, and more refined diagnostic practices for detecting HPV. Patients with HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer generally have a more favorable prognosis compared to those with HPV-negative disease. They tend to respond better to chemotherapy and radiotherapy (RT), are typically in better overall health with fewer comorbidities, whereas HPV-negative cases are often associated with chronic tobacco and alcohol use, which compromise physiological resilience. Furthermore, about 30% of HNC patients experience recurrence after treatment, with a 5-year survival rate of 51%. The incidence of HNC is higher among low-income and lower-educated groups, which is tied to their lack of health awareness and trouble getting medical help. Additionally, male patients tend to have lower survival rates than female patients, and factors such as age, race, and tumor staging significantly affect survival rates. Regarding treatment, a multidisciplinary team evaluation is crucial in determining the appropriate management strategy for head and neck squamous-cell carcinoma. Treatment plans vary significantly based on disease stage, anatomical location, and surgical accessibility. High-volume centers with extensive experience in multidisciplinary care are associated with improved outcomes and enhanced survival rates. Achieving structural and functional preservation, reducing treatment-related morbidity where possible, and maintaining long-term quality of life (QoL) require integrated care involving surgery, radiation oncology, and medical oncology, supported by ancillary services including dental and nutritional support, speech and language therapy, audiology, occupational and physical therapy, and psycho social counseling. RT plays a critical role in the treatment of HNC, which fundamentally relies on using high-energy radiation to damage the DNA of cancer cells, thereby slowing their growth. Common techniques for radiation therapy for HNC include three-dimensional conformal radiation therapy (3D-CRT), intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT), and stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT). These advancements have made it possible for RT to target tumors more precisely while minimizing damage to nearby healthy tissues, thereby lowering the incidence of side effects. For example, IMRT can deliver precise radiation to complex tumor shapes by adjusting the intensity and direction of the radiation beams, greatly improving local control rates and patients' QoL. RT to the head and neck region may cause adverse changes in surrounding tissues. Oral mucositis (OM) can range from white discoloration to erythematous ulcerative lesions, which may be secondarily infected by Candida species. Additionally, when major salivary glands are subjected to high RT doses, xerostomia becomes a concern. What’s more, HNC patients have a high risk of dental caries. The high incidence of caries is predominantly due to a compromised quantity and quality of saliva, a shift of oral flora in favor of cariogenic organisms, and dietary changes. Fibrosis of the jaw muscles often leads to restriction of jaw opening. In addition, irradiation damages bone-forming cells and compromises the vascularity of the bone. Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is the most devastating complication. Dental extractions as a result of dental caries place post-RT patients at risk of ORN with potentially serious consequences. These side effects may delay and interfere with cancer therapy, resulting in higher treatment expenses and worse QoL. While several reviews have touched upon this topic, they either failed to provide a comprehensive compilation of all available guidelines, or restricted their focus to a single, specific clinical question. Clinical practice guidelines provide systematic, evidence-based recommendations to assist clinicians and patients in healthcare decision-making. Increasingly integrated into routine medical practice, these guidelines are developed by health organizations and societies to offer concise instructions for disease prevention and treatment. Also, the implementation of guidelines aims to standardize clinical practice, minimize potential harm, and improve patient QoL. To fill this gap, this study represents the first to comprehensively synthesize existing clinical practice guidelines concerning oral diseases in HNC patients treated with RT.

These side effects may delay and interfere with cancer therapy, resulting in higher treatment expenses and worse QoL. While several reviews have touched upon this topic, they either failed to provide a comprehensive compilation of all available guidelines, or restricted their focus to a single, specific clinical question. Clinical practice guidelines provide systematic, evidence-based recommendations to assist clinicians and patients in healthcare decision-making. Increasingly integrated into routine medical practice, these guidelines are developed by health organizations and societies to offer concise instructions for disease prevention and treatment. Also, the implementation of guidelines aims to standardize clinical practice, minimize potential harm, and improve patient QoL. To fill this gap, this study represents the first to comprehensively synthesize existing clinical practice guidelines concerning oral diseases in HNC patients treated with RT.

source_records.title: Clinical Dental Guidelines for Patients with Head and Neck Cancer Treated with Radiotherapy: A Scoping Review
source_records.abstract: Head and neck cancer (HNC) remains a major global health concern, currently ranking as the seventh most common malignancy worldwide. Accounting for roughly 660,000 new cases and 325,000 deaths each year, the global burden of the disease is expected to grow by 30% by 2030. Squamous cell carcinomas (SCC) make up approximately 90% of all HNC cases, primarily originating from the mucosal lining of the oral cavity, pharynx, and larynx. Major risk factors for HNC include smoking, alcohol consumption, and infection with oncogenic viruses, such as human papillomavirus (HPV) for oropharyngeal cancer (HPVOC), and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) for nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC). HNCs are exhibiting a gradual decline in global incidence, partly attributable to the reduced consumption of tobacco. In contrast, the occurrence of HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer, primarily caused by HPV type 16, is rising, particularly among younger populations in North America and northern Europe. This upward trend is linked to greater clinical awareness, improved recognition of the relationship between HPV and HNCs, and more refined diagnostic practices for detecting HPV. Patients with HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer generally have a more favorable prognosis compared to those with HPV-negative disease. They tend to respond better to chemotherapy and radiotherapy (RT), are typically in better overall health with fewer comorbidities, whereas HPV-negative cases are often associated with chronic tobacco and alcohol use, which compromise physiological resilience. Furthermore, about 30% of HNC patients experience recurrence after treatment, with a 5-year survival rate of 51%. The incidence of HNC is higher among low-income and lower-educated groups, which is tied to their lack of health awareness and trouble getting medical help. Additionally, male patients tend to have lower survival rates than female patients, and factors such as age, race, and tumor staging significantly affect survival rates. Regarding treatment, a multidisciplinary team evaluation is crucial in determining the appropriate management strategy for head and neck squamous-cell carcinoma. Treatment plans vary significantly based on disease stage, anatomical location, and surgical accessibility. High-volume centers with extensive experience in multidisciplinary care are associated with improved outcomes and enhanced survival rates. Achieving structural and functional preservation, reducing treatment-related morbidity where possible, and maintaining long-term quality of life (QoL) require integrated care involving surgery, radiation oncology, and medical oncology, supported by ancillary services including dental and nutritional support, speech and language therapy, audiology, occupational and physical therapy, and psycho social counseling. RT plays a critical role in the treatment of HNC, which fundamentally relies on using high-energy radiation to damage the DNA of cancer cells, thereby slowing their growth. Common techniques for radiation therapy for HNC include three-dimensional conformal radiation therapy (3D-CRT), intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT), and stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT). These advancements have made it possible for RT to target tumors more precisely while minimizing damage to nearby healthy tissues, thereby lowering the incidence of side effects. For example, IMRT can deliver precise radiation to complex tumor shapes by adjusting the intensity and direction of the radiation beams, greatly improving local control rates and patients' QoL. RT to the head and neck region may cause adverse changes in surrounding tissues. Oral mucositis (OM) can range from white discoloration to erythematous ulcerative lesions, which may be secondarily infected by Candida species. Additionally, when major salivary glands are subjected to high RT doses, xerostomia becomes a concern. What’s more, HNC patients have a high risk of dental caries. The high incidence of caries is predominantly due to a compromised quantity and quality of saliva, a shift of oral flora in favor of cariogenic organisms, and dietary changes. Fibrosis of the jaw muscles often leads to restriction of jaw opening. In addition, irradiation damages bone-forming cells and compromises the vascularity of the bone. Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is the most devastating complication. Dental extractions as a result of dental caries place post-RT patients at risk of ORN with potentially serious consequences. These side effects may delay and interfere with cancer therapy, resulting in higher treatment expenses and worse QoL. While several reviews have touched upon this topic, they either failed to provide a comprehensive compilation of all available guidelines, or restricted their focus to a single, specific clinical question. Clinical practice guidelines provide systematic, evidence-based recommendations to assist clinicians and patients in healthcare decision-making. Increasingly integrated into routine medical practice, these guidelines are developed by health organizations and societies to offer concise instructions for disease prevention and treatment. Also, the implementation of guidelines aims to standardize clinical practice, minimize potential harm, and improve patient QoL. To fill this gap, this study represents the first to comprehensively synthesize existing clinical practice guidelines concerning oral diseases in HNC patients treated with RT.

title: The Relationship between Serum Selenium Levels and The Occurrence of Eye Tumors
abstract: Eye tumors are serious diseases with high morbidity and mortality rates. Risk factors include UV-B radiation, immune system disorders, smoking, HPV infection, p53 gene mutations, and free radical exposure. Selenium, an antioxidant through selenoproteins, serves as a chemoprotective agent against cancer. This case–control study was conducted to evaluate the association between serum selenium levels and eye tumors at RS Prof. Universitas Sumatera Utara from June to July 2024. The study included 20 eye tumor patients and 20 controls, with 11 females and 9 males in each group. The mean age was 43.55 years in the tumor group and 41.65 years in controls. In the eye tumor group, 45% were overweight, while 55% of the control group were normoweight. Among tumor patients, 65% had benign and 35% had malignant lesions. Serum selenium levels were significantly lower in the tumor group than in controls (100.03 ± 27.93 μg/L vs 213.15 ± 33.09 μg/L; p 0.001). Patients with malignant tumors had lower selenium levels than those with benign tumors (87.37 ± 30.68 vs 106.84 ± 24.91 μg/L). Selenium levels were significantly associated with body mass index in tumor patients (p = 0.036), but not in controls (p = 0.083).

title: ZNF395, the Transcriptional Factor Linked to Viral, Inflammatory and Cancer Processes
abstract: Background/Objectives: ZNF395, also known as PBF (Human Papillomavirus Binding Factor), is an intrinsically disordered cellular protein involved in critical biological processes. These include human papillomavirus replication, the innate immune response, apoptosis induction, cell growth inhibition, the activation of autologous cytotoxic T lymphocytes, and prognosis in various cancers—all of which are associated with diseases of global significance. ZNF395 has been differentially associated with the replication of HPV8, HIV, CMV, and EBV. Notably, reports indicate contrasting behaviors across different cancer types, suggesting that it could act as a tumor suppressor or serve as a marker for poor prognosis. Furthermore, hypoxic conditions induce ZNF395 expression through the activation of HIF-1α and NF-κB, resulting in increased IL-6 and IL-8 levels in response to cellular stress, thereby promoting cell survival, migration, and angiogenesis. Methods: A non-systematic literature search was performed in PubMed (2000–2026) using keywords related to ZNF395, cancer, and viruses. Conclusions: In this work, we summarize the diverse functions performed by this single protein, challenging the traditional “one structure, one function” paradigm. Most importantly, our findings highlight that ZNF395 may hold significant potential for the diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment of cancer.
authors: Luis Niño de Rivera Y Oyarzabal

title: Evaluation of the Educational Effects of Cervical Cancer and HPV Vaccine Education for Junior High School Students 中学生を対象とした子宮頸がん・HPVワクチンに関する教育効果の検証
abstract: BACKGROUND In Japan, human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rates declined markedly after the suspension of proactive governmental recommendation in 2013. Reports on school pharmacist-led cervical cancer and HPV vaccination education remain limited. This study evaluated the effects of lectures on cervical cancer and HPV vaccination delivered by school pharmacists to junior high school students on knowledge, awareness, and willingness to receive HPV vaccination. METHODS A before-after study was conducted among students from four public junior high schools in Shinagawa City, Tokyo, Japan. School pharmacists delivered a 45-min lecture, and anonymous questionnaire surveys were conducted before and after the lecture. Changes before and after the lecture were analyzed using McNemar's test, and factors associated with willingness to receive HPV vaccination were examined using multivariable logistic regression analysis. RESULTS A total of 216 students were included in the analysis. After the lecture, knowledge and awareness regarding cervical cancer, HPV, and HPV vaccination significantly improved (all p<0.001). In addition, the proportion of students who answered that they "wanted to receive the HPV vaccine" significantly increased from 16.7 to 45.8% (p<0.001). Multivariable analysis showed that pre-lecture interest in cervical cancer, post-lecture knowledge regarding the HPV vaccine, interest in the lecture, and changes in impressions toward vaccines were significantly associated with willingness to receive HPV vaccination. CONCLUSIONS Educational interventions delivered by school pharmacists may contribute to improving knowledge and awareness among junior high school students and increasing willingness to receive HPV vaccination.

title: Prognostic value of dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI and plasma angiogenic markers for survival outcomes in HPV-negative oropharyngeal carcinoma treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy
abstract: PURPOSE: Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) enables non-invasive assessment of tumour vascularity, while circulating angiogenic factors may reflect tumour-associated angiogenic activity. We investigated whether DCE-MRI perfusion parameters and plasma angiogenic factors measured before and early during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) are associated with survival in human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). METHODS: In this prospective single-centre study, 24 patients with locally advanced HPV-negative OPSCC treated with cCRT were analysed. DCE-MRI perfusion parameters (Ktrans, Kep, Ve, iAUC) were analysed at baseline and early intra-treatment (20 Gy), while plasma angiogenic factors (vascular endothelial growth factor [VEGF], connective tissue growth factor, platelet-derived growth factor-AB, angiogenin, endostatin, and thrombospondin-1) were analysed at baseline, early intra-treatment and post-treatment (10-12 weeks). Disease-specific survival (DSS) was assessed using univariable Cox regression (hazard ratios [HRs] per 1-SD) and Kaplan-Meier analysis with false-discovery-rate correction. RESULTS: Seven patients died of the index cancer. Higher baseline Ktrans (HR per 1-SD 0.30, p = 0.031) and higher early intra-treatment plasma VEGF (HR 0.37, p = 0.043) were nominally associated with better DSS; VEGF also showed separation in Kaplan-Meier analysis (3-year DSS 92% vs. 36%, log-rank p = 0.016). Effect estimates were similar after exploratory adjustment for tumour volume but attenuated after adjustment for stage. No association remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction, and the early VEGF association partly overlapped with local treatment response. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, baseline DCE-MRI perfusion (Ktrans) and plasma VEGF showed hypothesis-generating associations with DSS in HPV-negative OPSCC. As no association survived multiplicity correction, these findings require validation in larger independent cohorts.

title: Computational Identification of the Binding Mechanism of a Flagellin-Fabricated Chimeric Peptide Vaccine that Targets the Innate and Adaptive Immune Systems Against Cervix Papilloma
abstract: Flagellin activates innate, cellular and humoral immunity through Toll-like receptor 5 (TLR5), and this interaction can be exploited to improve vaccines against oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV). The binding mechanism between flagellin-fabricated peptide vaccines (FFPVs) and TLR5, however, remains unclear. Here, three FFPV candidates (C58, C52 and C16) were designed from overlapped epitope segments in the conserved N-terminal region of the L2 minor capsid protein of HPV58, HPV52 and HPV16. These segments were predicted to induce cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, T-helper, IFNγ and B-cell responses. Each construct also carried two TLR agonist adjuvants (flagellin and RS09), two universal T-helper epitopes and defined peptide linkers. Physicochemical and immunological properties were evaluated, and three-dimensional models of the FFPVs and TLR5 were generated, refined and validated. Protein–protein docking with HADDOCK and PRODIGY ranked the TLR5-C58 complex highest, ahead of TLR5-C16 and TLR5-C52. To test the docking result, the TLR5-C58 complex was simulated for [100 ns] in explicit solvent, and the root mean square deviation, total energy, hydrogen bonds and key-residue distances were analyzed. The simulation identified a binding mode with ten key residues in the leucine-rich repeat (LRR) region of TLR5, and the binding free energies agreed with experimental reports. These findings offer a structural basis for the rational design of L2-based vaccines against cervical cancer.

title: 525 Open-label study of zopapogene imadenovec-drba retreatment and vector shedding evaluation in adult patients with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
abstract: Background Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) is a rare, neoplastic disorder caused by chronic infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) type 6 or 11. Repeat surgical debulking has been the most common treatment for RRP. Zopapogene imadenovec-drba (zopa), a novel adenovector-based immunotherapy, is the first and only FDA-approved treatment for adults with RRP. In the pivotal study, robust efficacy was observed following zopa treatment with 51% (34 to 69; 95% CI) of patients achieving a complete response (CR). 83% (15/18) of patients that achieved a CR at 12 months (m) remained in CR after a duration of follow-up of at least 36m (range: 36-51m). Zopa was well-tolerated with no serious adverse events and no grade >2 treatment-related adverse events. Neutralizing antibody (NAb) titers collected up to 52-weeks post-treatment remained at low to undetectable levels and there was no correlation between NAb titer and clinical response. Zopa is recommended as first-line treatment for adults with RRP in an RRP Foundation position statement.1 One cohort of the following ongoing study will evaluate the presence of vector shedding in adults with RRP who had no prior zopa treatment. Another cohort aims to determine whether retreatment with zopa can eliminate the need for subsequent papilloma debulking procedures in adults with RRP.Methods This trial ( NCT06538480) is an open-label, multi-center, study enrolling patients in two cohorts. The primary endpoint of the first cohort will evaluate the magnitude and duration of zopa vector shedding for up to 6 weeks in 10 patients with no prior exposure to zopa. Another cohort will evaluate the safety and efficacy of zopa in 20 patients with RRP, who have previously received zopa treatment. The primary endpoint of the retreatment cohort is the rate of CR, defined as the percentage of patients with no requirement for surgery in the 12m following treatment completion. Key endpoints include time to the first post-treatment debulking procedure after retreatment completion, vocal function change, extent of papilloma growth, and induction of HPV-specific T cell responses. Patients must be ≥18 years old with a clinical diagnosis of RRP irrespective of the number of prior surgeries, satisfactory organ function, ECOG 0-1, and the presence of laryngotracheal papillomas. Exclusion criteria: active autoimmune disease, steroid use >10mg prednisolone-equivalent daily, pregnancy or uncontrolled illness.Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06538480Reference Best SR, Friedman AD, Rosen CA, et al. title: Infectious disease risk awareness and protective behaviors among adult emergency department patients: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to assess awareness of infectious disease risks and preventive behaviours among adults presenting to emergency departments with suspected infectious diseases. METHODS: This multicenter descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted between February and March 2026 in four university-affiliated emergency departments in Istanbul. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews with 250 adults using the Patient Information Form and the Communicable Diseases Risk Awareness and Protection Scale. Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis tests, Spearman's rank correlation analysis, and effect-size estimates were used. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: The mean CDRAPS total score was 143.01 ± 14.47 (median, 144; range, 85-180). Significant differences in CDRAPS total scores were observed according to mode of arrival, HPV vaccination, smoking, alcohol use, healthcare work reported as an epidemiological risk factor, and isolation type (all p < 0.05); effect sizes for these comparisons were small. Fatigue, pain, fever, and cough were the most common presenting complaints. These findings indicate variation in infectious disease risk awareness and protective behaviours according to selected behavioural, healthcare-related, and infection-control characteristics. CONCLUSION: Infectious disease risk awareness and protective behaviours among emergency department patients varied according to selected behavioural, healthcare-related, and infection-control characteristics. These findings may inform the development and evaluation of patient-centred infection prevention and risk communication strategies integrated into routine emergency care.

title: 524 Zopapogene imadenovec-drba, a novel adenovector-based immunotherapy, induces complete and durable responses in recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
abstract: Background Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) is a rare, neoplastic disorder caused by chronic human papillomavirus (HPV) type 6 or 11 infection. Repeat surgical debulking has historically been the most common treatment for RRP symptom management. Zopapogene imadenovec-drba (zopa), a novel adenoviral vector-based immunotherapy, is the first and only FDA-approved treatment for adults with RRP. Zopa is now recommended as the first-line treatment for adults with RRP in an RRP Foundation position statement authored by 16 key opinion leaders.1Methods The pivotal trial ( NCT04724980) evaluated zopa in patients with RRP requiring ≥3 clinically indicated interventions 12 months (m) prior to treatment. 12m follow-up data was reported and demonstrated that 4 subcutaneous injections of zopa (5 x 1011 particle units per injection; n = 35) were well-tolerated, with no serious adverse events, no grade >2 treatment-related adverse events, and no early treatment discontinuations. The most common adverse events were injection-site reaction, fatigue, chills, fever, and myalgia.Robust efficacy was observed following zopa treatment with 51% (34 to 69; 95% CI) of patients achieving a complete response (CR), defined as no requirement for interventions in the 12m following treatment. Here we present data up to 51m of follow-up.Results As of April 30, 2026, with a duration of follow-up of at least 36m (range: 36-51m), 83% (15/18) of patients who achieved a CR at 12m remain in CR with no recurrence of papilloma requiring surgical or medical intervention. Out of the 15 patients remaining in CR, 5 patients have reached 4 years of follow-up.No new safety events were observed during long-term follow-up.Zopa treatment results in the generation of HPV-specific T cell mediated immune responses which was assessed by IFN-y ELISpot assay. The induction of HPV-specific T cells at the time of treatment completion was significantly higher in patients that achieved a CR or a reduction in the requirement for surgical interventions in the 12 months after treatment (mean fold-change 165 vs. 5, P < 0.018).Conclusions Zopa treatment demonstrated significant clinical benefit with the vast majority of CR patients experiencing ongoing durable complete responses for up to 4 years with excellent long-term safety. Updated results will be available at the time of presentation.Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04724980.Reference Best SR, Friedman AD, Rosen CA, et al. Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis foundation position statement on the management of adults With RRP. title: Split-T7 transcriptional promoter encoding molecular logic circuit for versatile cell-free diagnostics
abstract: Cell-free systems are promising tools for molecular diagnostics, yet they remain limited by low multiplexing capacity and background interference. Here, a multiplex cell-free diagnostic platform termed BOLT (Bi-locked Orchestrated Logic-triggered Transcription amplification platform) has been developed by a split-T7 transcriptional promoter strategy. BOLT encodes a molecular logic circuit by locking the split T7 promoter fragments within independent programmable metastable hairpins. Target-triggered strand displacement serves as the circuit input, simultaneously unlocking these conformational gates to drive the output of promoter assembly. The bi-locked design strictly suppresses background leakage by raising the thermodynamic barrier against spontaneous assembly, thereby ensuring the reconstituted promoter drives orthogonal RNA aptamer transcription for crosstalk-free multiplexing. BOLT achieved HPV16 and HPV18 genotyping within 1 h, with femtomolar sensitivity and high qPCR concordance in cervical swab samples, demonstrating ≥96.3% sensitivity and 100% specificity. This split-promoter logic strategy provides a programmable framework for high-fidelity multiplexed cell-free diagnostics.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of AI-Assisted Colposcopy for Detection of Cervical Precancerous Lesions at Buddhachinaraj Hospital
abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted colposcopy imaging system for detecting cervical precancerous lesions (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN)) CIN2+ and CIN1+ compared with conventional colposcopy. Materials and Methods: This prospective diagnostic accuracy study included women aged 25–60 years who had abnormal human papillomavirus (HPV) screening results requiring colposcopic evaluation at Buddhachinaraj Phitsanulok Hospital. The primary outcome was the diagnostic accuracy of AI-assisted versus conventional colposcopy for detecting CIN2+ lesions; the secondary outcome was diagnostic accuracy for detecting CIN1+ lesions. A total of 165 women underwent colposcopy. Histopathological findings from cervical biopsies served as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), accuracy, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results: The mean age of participants was 39.5 ± 8.3 years. Histopathological examination identified CIN1 in 50.3% and CIN2+ lesions in 41.8% of participants. For CIN2+, AI-assisted colposcopy had an accuracy of 69.1%, sensitivity of 26.1%, specificity of 100%, PPV of 100%, and NPV of 65.3%, whereas conventional colposcopy had an accuracy of 77.6%, sensitivity of 50.7%, specificity of 96.9%, PPV of 92.1%, and NPV of 73.2%. The AUROC was 0.630 for AI-assisted colposcopy and 0.738 for conventional colposcopy. For CIN1+, AI-assisted colposcopy demonstrated an accuracy of 84.8%, sensitivity of 84.9%, specificity of 84.6%, PPV of 98.5%, and NPV of 32.4%, compared with 88.5%, 88.8%, 84.6%, 98.5%, and 39.3%, respectively, for conventional colposcopy. The AUROC values were 0.847 and 0.867 for AI-assisted and conventional colposcopy, respectively.Conclusion: AI-assisted colposcopy demonstrated less diagnostic performance for CIN2+ compared with conventional colposcopy but comparable performance for CIN1+. AI-assisted colposcopy should therefore be considered an adjunct to, rather than a replacement for, conventional colposcopic assessment in clinical practice.

The primary outcome was the diagnostic accuracy of AI-assisted versus conventional colposcopy for detecting CIN2+ lesions; the secondary outcome was diagnostic accuracy for detecting CIN1+ lesions. A total of 165 women underwent colposcopy. Histopathological findings from cervical biopsies served as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), accuracy, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results: The mean age of participants was 39.5 ± 8.3 years. Histopathological examination identified CIN1 in 50.3% and CIN2+ lesions in 41.8% of participants. For CIN2+, AI-assisted colposcopy had an accuracy of 69.1%, sensitivity of 26.1%, specificity of 100%, PPV of 100%, and NPV of 65.3%, whereas conventional colposcopy had an accuracy of 77.6%, sensitivity of 50.7%, specificity of 96.9%, PPV of 92.1%, and NPV of 73.2%. The AUROC was 0.630 for AI-assisted colposcopy and 0.738 for conventional colposcopy. For CIN1+, AI-assisted colposcopy demonstrated an accuracy of 84.8%, sensitivity of 84.9%, specificity of 84.6%, PPV of 98.5%, and NPV of 32.4%, compared with 88.5%, 88.8%, 84.6%, 98.5%, and 39.3%, respectively, for conventional colposcopy. The AUROC values were 0.847 and 0.867 for AI-assisted and conventional colposcopy, respectively.Conclusion: AI-assisted colposcopy demonstrated less diagnostic performance for CIN2+ compared with conventional colposcopy but comparable performance for CIN1+. AI-assisted colposcopy should therefore be considered an adjunct to, rather than a replacement for, conventional colposcopic assessment in clinical practice.

abstract: Abstract Purpose: Human papillomavirus (HPV)–associated carcinomas (HPV + cancers) account for 5% of all cancers. Circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) assays for HPV + cancer surveillance have limited prognostic utility at the time of cancer diagnosis. Although HPV integration into the host genome is a proven tissue-based biomarker predicting poor clinical outcomes, existing clinically utilized ctHPVDNA assays cannot classify the viral physical state. Experimental Design: We previously developed HPV-DeepSeek, a multifeature HPV whole-genome sequencing liquid biopsy with 99% diagnostic accuracy at the time of HPV + oropharyngeal cancer diagnosis. We tested the diagnostic accuracy of HPV-DeepSeek in a cohort of 235 HPV + cancers across 9 anatomic sites and used a novel blood-based computational classifier to infer the HPV genome physical state from plasma, termed HPV sequencing-based integration analysis (HPV-SIGNAL), to assess its prognostic potential. Results: HPV-DeepSeek achieved 99% sensitivity and specificity. In 189 eligible samples, HPV-SIGNAL identified 4 viral physical states: episomal-only ( n = 71), episomal-rearranged ( n = 52), integrated-mixed ( n = 57), and integrated-clonal ( n = 9), which were confirmed and further elucidated via 3 orthogonal tissue and blood approaches. Patients harboring integrated viral states in blood exhibited significantly worse age-adjusted and American Joint Committee on Cancer stage–adjusted progression-free survival [PFS; HR, 2.78; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.30–5.99; P = 0.009] and overall survival (OS; HR, 2.95; 95% CI, 1.01–8.61; P = 0.048) compared with patients with episomal states. Conclusions: HPV whole-genome sequencing liquid biopsy has high diagnostic accuracy across HPV + cancer types and can be used to identify and classify HPV physical states from blood. Patients with integrated viral states detected in blood demonstrated worse PFS and OS, suggesting that blood-based HPV physical state classification could be used as a prognostic tool at the time of cancer diagnosis.

title: 364 Selective expansion of T-cell receptor-engineered T cells using an IL-2 cis-targeted antibody
abstract: Background T-cell receptor (TCR)-T cell therapy has demonstrated clinical activity across multiple human malignancies. IL-2 is used during cell manufacturing and following infusion to support T cell expansion. However, IL-2 activates all T cell subsets, resulting in significant clinical toxicity. We developed bifunctional molecules (cis-IL-2) comprising antibody against mouse TCRβ constant region (H57), which is incorporated into engineered TCR-T cells, linked with human IL-2, to selectively deliver IL-2 to engineered T cells.Methods Engineered T cells targeting HPV16 E7 or NY-Eso-1 were treated with cis-IL-2 in various culture conditions with or without exogenous IL-2. T cell phenotype and function were evaluated by flow cytometry and tumor cytotoxicity assays. In vivo efficacy of E7 TCR-T cells pretreated with cis-IL-2 was assessed in the SS4050 (HPV16 E7+/HLA-A*02+) xenograft mouse model.Results In NY-Eso-1 T cells, cis-IL-2 increased the subset of CD8 +NY-Eso-1 T cells from 35% to 82%, compared with 35% to 44% using H57 plus soluble IL-2. Similarly, cis-IL2 drove robust expansion of CD8+ E7TCR T-cells without exogenous IL-2, increasing from baseline 15% to 47%, 75%, 86% on days 4, 7, and 11, respectively. Functionally, E7 TCR-T cells pretreated with cis-IL-2 exhibited enhanced tumor recognition and cytotoxicity, producing higher levels of IFN-g following co-culture with HPV16 E7+/HLA-A*02+ tumor lines (SS4050 and Caski). In vivo, cis-IL-2 pretreated E7 TCR T-cells significantly improved tumor control in SS4050 xenograft model, resulting in tumor clearance in 3 of 5 mice compared with none in untransduced or non-treated E7TCR T-cells without evidence of toxicity.Conclusions Cis-IL-2 selectively delivered IL-2 to engineered TCR-T cells, resulting in enhanced antitumor efficacy both in vitro and in vivo. This approach minimizes off-target effects associated with conventional IL-2 administration and provides a promising strategy to improve the safety and effectiveness of TCR-T cell therapies for cancer patients.

title: A Case Series on Integrated Management of Anal Condyloma Acuminata
abstract: Anal Condyloma acuminata is a viral disease caused by Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) which is distinct from virus of the common wart. It is usually associated to other veneral diseases and immune-compromised state. Certain strains of HPV are associated to dysplasia and progression to cancer usually squamous cell carcinoma of the anus. Patient usually present with mass per anum, itching and false odour rarely, relentless growth results in giant condylomata (Buschke Löwenstein tumour), which may obliterate the anal orifice. Method: Five patients of anal condyloma acuminata were managed by excision with electrocauterization and the excised masses were sent for histopathological examination to rule out any malignancy. In the post-operative period dressing was done with Jatyadi Taila and also Ayurvedic oral medicines were prescribed to enhance wound healing. Result: All the patients were cured without recurrences till the date. No patients had significant post-operative adverse events. Histopathological examination turned out to be non-malignant for all the patients. The treatment was well tolerated and was affordable to all the patients. Discussion: There are various methods for managing condyloma acuminata, out of which electrocoagulation is considered as best strategy of management where first or at most second degree of burn is created. title: Anorectal care products cause variable inflammation and adverse barrier effects in a mucosal epithelial model
abstract: Introduction: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and colorectal cancer (CRC) are rising in the United States, yet their shared mucosal environment remains underexplored. Rectal douching, a common practice among individuals engaging in receptive anal intercourse, has been epidemiologically linked to increased STI and HPV risk, but biological mechanisms are unclear. Methods: Using a human colorectal epithelial co-culture model (Caco-2/HT29-MTX-E12), we compared the effects of common douching products on cell viability, barrier integrity, and cytokine response. Results: Hyperosmolar or surfactant-containing solutions, including saline enemas, detergents, and soaps, caused rapid declines in metabolic activity and transepithelial electrical resistance, coupled with IL-6 and TNF-α upregulation. In contrast, isotonic formulations maintained epithelial viability and barrier function comparable to buffered controls while reducing inflammatory signaling. Discussion: These findings provide mechanistic evidence that many consumer douching products compromise mucosal health and highlight the feasibility of harm-reduction designs for safer anal hygiene and sexual preparation.

title: Phytochemical Characterization, Electronic Reactivity and Anticancer Evaluation of Symphyotrichum novi-belgii
abstract: Background: Symphyotrichum novi-belgii (syn. Aster novi-belgii) belongs to the Asteraceae family and remains comparatively underexplored from a phytochemical and pharmacological perspective. Symphyotrichum novi-belgii remains poorly characterized in terms of organ-specific phytochemistry and anticancer relevance. Methods: In this study, methanolic extracts of the leaves, stems and roots of Symphyotrichum novi-belgii were characterized using FTIR and GC-MS. Selected phytoconstituents were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and molecular docking against HPV16 E6, while the effects of the crude extracts on HeLa cervical cancer cells were assessed using the MTT cell-viability assay following treatment with each extract at 100 μg/mL for 48 h. The chemical and computational findings were considered alongside the MTT cell-viability results to compare the leaf (Lf), stem (St) and root (Rt) extracts of S. novi-belgii and identify phytoconstituents warranting further investigation. Results: FTIR spectra revealed hydroxyl, carbonyl, aromatic, aliphatic, and C-O/C-O-C functionalities. GC-MS detected nine chromatographic features each in the Lf and St extracts and seven in the Rt extract, representing chemical classes such as organic and phenolic acids, flavonoid-type compounds, terpenoids, an alkaloid, nitrogen-containing heterocycles, lactones, ethers, and a fatty-acid ester. DFT calculations on selected proposed molecular structures indicated the highest calculated molecular softness for the sanguinarine model (Lf8; 0.831 eV−1) and the highest electrophilicity index for the caftaric-acid model (Rt6; 4.356 eV). Separately, the proposed flavonol-type molecular structure represented by Lf5 (leaf), St6 (stem), and Rt4 (root) was distinct from the sanguinarine model (Lf8). The original docking calculations reported predicted binding scores of −10.4 kcal/mol for the Lf5 and Rt4 model entries. However, discrepancies between the original library-search results and the corresponding literature-assisted GC-MS assignments prevent confirmation that these molecular structures were present in the extracts. The computational results therefore represent theoretical predictions for the selected structures rather than verified properties of experimentally identified plant constituents. In the preliminary MTT evaluation at 100 μg/mL following 48 h of exposure, the Lf extract showed 31.03% inhibition, whereas the Rt and St extracts yielded −12.98% and −10.61%, respectively. None of the extracts reached 50% inhibition at the concentration tested. Because no concentration–response series was performed, extract-specific IC50 values could not be determined. Doxorubicin, included as the positive drug control, showed 81.81% apparent MTT inhibition under the reported single-concentration conditions. Conclusions: FTIR and exploratory GC-MS analyses revealed differences in the detectable chemical features of the three extracts, while DFT and molecular docking provided theoretical predictions for selected proposed molecular structures. At 100 μg/mL following 48 h of exposure, the leaf (Lf) extract showed a higher apparent MTT percentage-inhibition value than the root (Rt) and stem (St) extracts. This single-concentration observation is descriptive and does not establish statistically significant differences, cytotoxicity, or anticancer efficacy.

title: Closing the Cancer Data Gap: Development of the CARIFAS Tool for Cancer Risk Factor Surveillance in Uganda
abstract: PURPOSE Cancer incidence is rising in Uganda. While some life-style risks are documented, key cancer drivers, including infections, environmental and occupational exposures remain inadequately measured. The aim of the study was to develop a standardized, scalable cancer risk factor surveillance tool (CARIFAS Tool) tailored for low- and middle-income countries. METHODS The CARIFAS Tool was developed between 2022 and 2024 based on the WHO STEPwise approach, a literature review, and a Delphi consensus process to ensure content and face validity. The process included three multi-sectoral harmonization workshops and a population-based cross-sectional survey conducted in Mayuge district (n = 240, ≥18 years). Data was analysed using STATA 15. RESULTS The tool introduces three key innovations: inclusion of reproductive, environmental, occupational, and infection-related cancer risk factors; localization of alcohol measures to improve contextual relevance; and adoption of the Alternative Healthy Eating Index to assess unhealthy diet. Prevalence estimates from the tool agree with existing literature: tobacco use (5.7%), alcohol use (10.2%), physical inactivity (15.3%), overweight (17.3%), and obesity (6.3%). 70% had unhealthy diet. 43.6% reported occupational exposures, and 12 % reported high to medium environmental exposures to diesel motor emissions, while 99.4% reported exposure to cooking/wood smoke. Reproductive risk indicators showed that 78.9% reported menarche above 12 years, 92.2% had their first birth below 25 years, the mean parity was 6 children per woman, 2.0% were nulliparous, 71.1% breastfed for 12–24 months, and 21.6% had used oral contraception. Infections findings included HIV (Male 1.4% and 2.9% in females), Hepatitis-B (Males is 0.45% and Females 1.05%), Hepatitis-C (male 4.7% and 1.0% in women), H. pylori (Males 17% and Females 18.4%), and HPV (17.6% among women). Importantly, this work led to the establishment of a multi-sectoral network and framework, including the Ministry of Health (MOH), Uganda Cancer Institute (UCI), Uganda Bureau of Statistics (UBOS), Makerere University (MAK), major hospitals, HCIVs, and Village Health Teams (VHTs), demonstrating feasibility for national scale-up. CONCLUSION The CARIFAS Tool is a feasible, context-appropriate, scalable approach to standardized cancer risk factor surveillance. With national integration, this model provides a practical pathway for strengthening cancer data systems in Uganda and other similar settings.

title: ĐẶC ĐIỂM HÌNH ẢNH SOI CỔ TỬ CUNG Ở PHỤ NỮ NHIỄM HPV TYPE NGUY CƠ CAO TẠI BỆNH VIỆN ĐA KHOA QUỐC TẾ VINMEC TIMES CITY
abstract: Mục tiêu: Mô tả đặc điểm hình ảnh soi cổ tử cung và khảo sát mối liên quan giữa nhóm HPV16/18 với mức độ bất thường trên soi cổ tử cung ở phụ nữ nhiễm HPV type nguy cơ cao. Đối tượng và phương pháp: Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang trên 57 phụ nữ nhiễm HPV type nguy cơ cao được soi cổ tử cung tại Bệnh viện Đa khoa Quốc tế Vinmec Times City từ tháng 01 đến tháng 12 năm 2025. Kết quả: Tuổi trung bình là 34,7 ± 7,9 tuổi. Có 54/57 trường hợp (94,7%) được đánh giá đầy đủ theo tiêu chí soi cổ tử cung của nghiên cứu; SCJ quan sát hoàn toàn ở 45 trường hợp (78,9%). TZ1, TZ2 và TZ3 lần lượt chiếm 35,1%, 43,9% và 21,1%. Hình ảnh soi cổ tử cung bất thường được ghi nhận ở 43/57 trường hợp (75,4%). Biểu mô trắng sau bôi acid acetic là dấu hiệu thường gặp nhất (39/57; 68,4%), tiếp theo là chấm đáy mảnh (24,6%) và khảm mảnh (19,3%). title: Optimising HPV Vaccination for Cervical Cancer Prevention in Women Living with HIV: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis Across 13 African Countries
abstract: **Background:** Women living with HIV face a substantially higher risk of persistent HPV infection and cervical cancer, yet HPV vaccination strategies targeting this high-risk population remain limited in many low- and middle-income countries. We evaluated the lifetime health impact and cost-effectiveness of HIV-targeted HPV vaccination strategies across 13 sub-Saharan African countries. **Methods:** We developed an age-structured Markov model of HPV infection and cervical cancer in a closed cohort of 100,000 females, stratified by HIV status, and calibrated it separately for each country to age-specific cervical cancer incidence, cervical cancer mortality, and female HIV prevalence. Six HIV-targeted strategies were compared with routine two-dose vaccination at age 14 years. The strategies either provided a booster dose to previously vaccinated WLHIV or combined a booster for previously vaccinated WLHIV with a three-dose primary catch-up course for previously unvaccinated WLHIV. Interventions were delivered at ages 18 or 24 years under standard- and high-coverage assumptions. Outcomes included cervical cancer cases averted, cervical cancer deaths averted among WLHIV, discounted disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) averted, additional physical vaccine doses, and incremental costs from the health-system and vaccination-programme perspectives. **Results:** All HIV-targeted vaccination strategies reduced cervical cancer burden relative to routine vaccination across the 13 countries. Higher-coverage strategies generally produced greater health gains, with mean DALYs averted ranging from 9.05 for booster vaccination at age 24 years to 88.42 for high-coverage combined booster and catch-up vaccination at age 24 years. However, the relative performance of vaccination at ages 18 and 24 varied across strategies and countries. Booster-only strategies achieved the greatest health gains per additional vaccine dose, while combined strategies at higher coverage produced larger overall benefits. From the health-system perspective, 68 of 78 country-strategy comparisons were more effective and less costly than routine vaccination after accounting for avoided cervical cancer treatment costs. From the vaccination-programme perspective, all strategies required additional expenditure. **Conclusions:** Targeted HPV vaccination among women living with HIV can reduce cervical cancer burden and may be cost-saving when avoided treatment costs are considered. Higher-coverage combined strategies produced the greatest overall health gains, while booster-only strategies were more dose-efficient, supporting context-specific vaccination decisions.

title: A randomized clinical trial comparing visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) to Pocket Colposcopy for the triage of HPV+ women living with HIV in Kisumu, Kenya.
abstract: Abstract Objective The World Health Organization recommends a “screen, triage, treat” approach for cervical cancer screening for Women Living with HIV (WLWH) in resource-limited settings, with Human Papillomavirus (HPV) testing preferred for screening. We assessed the use of the Pocket colposcope as an adjunct tool to Visual Assessment with Acetic Acid (VIA) for the triage of HPV+ WLWH. Methods We carried out a randomized clinical trial across six clinics in Kisumu, Kenya between November 2022 and April 2023 ( NCT04998318 ). WLWH who screened positive with self-collected HPV were randomized to either the VIA or Pocket arm. Exam positivity was determined by presence or absence of aceto-white epithelium (AWE). Directed biopsies were performed on AWE; if negative, two random biopsies were taken. Pathology was used to determine diagnostic accuracy. Providers and participants took brief surveys after each exam. Findings The rate of a positive exams was 17.3% for VIA compared to 14.3% for the Pocket. source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The WHO recommends a "screen, triage, treat" approach for cervical cancer screening for Women Living with HIV (WLWH) in resource-limited settings, with HPV testing preferred for screening. We sought to compare Visual Assessment with Acetic Acid (VIA) assisted with the Pocket Colposcope to naked eye VIA for triage of HPV + WLWH. METHODS: In a randomized clinical trial across six clinics in Kisumu, Kenya (November 2022 to June 2023), HPV + WLWH were randomized to VIA or Pocket colposcopy. Exam positivity was determined by presence of aceto-white epithelium (AWE); biopsies were taken from AWE or randomly if negative. Diagnostic accuracy was confirmed with pathology. Both providers and patients found the Pocket acceptable for triage. CONCLUSION: The Pocket colposcope detected more treatable disease and reduced overtreatment. This study shows the Pocket colposcope is a feasible, lower-cost device that could facilitate biopsy confirmation, increase provider training, improve patient education, and enable remote diagnosis.

title: Trust in HPV vaccine effectiveness and safety and willingness to initiate HPV vaccination among unvaccinated female college students recruited through university-based online networks in China: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an important strategy for preventing cervical cancer and other HPV-related diseases. Vaccine trust may encompass distinct perceptions of effectiveness and safety. This study examined cross-sectional associations of trust in HPV vaccine effectiveness and safety with HPV vaccination willingness among unvaccinated female college students recruited through university-based online networks in China. Methods This cross-sectional online survey recruited female college students from 24 universities located in 12 provincial-level administrative regions of China between January 2025 and March 2026. The primary analysis included participants who reported no prior HPV vaccination. High willingness was defined as reporting being somewhat willing or very willing to receive HPV vaccination. Trust in HPV vaccine effectiveness, the safety of domestically produced bivalent HPV vaccines, and the safety of imported HPV vaccines were modeled as categorical variables. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Among 2,215 unvaccinated participants, 818 (36.9%) reported high HPV vaccination willingness. Higher categories of effectiveness trust and safety trust were associated with greater odds of reporting high willingness. Compared with participants who were very distrustful of HPV vaccine effectiveness, those who were very trustful had an aOR of 5.397 (95% CI 3.246–8.973). The corresponding aORs for being very trustful of the safety of domestically produced bivalent HPV vaccines and imported HPV vaccines were 3.307 (95% CI 1.930–5.665) and 5.022 (95% CI 2.741–9.201), respectively. Associations were directionally consistent after excluding participants reporting uncertain willingness. Conclusions Among unvaccinated female college students recruited through university-based online networks in 12 provinces in China, higher self-reported trust in HPV vaccine effectiveness and safety was associated with greater reported willingness to initiate HPV vaccination. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to examine whether approaches addressing effectiveness and safety concerns improve HPV vaccine uptake.

title: 307 A sparse epitope-HLA interface for HPV oncoprotein-specific T cells
abstract: Background Human papillomavirus 16 (HPV16) oncoproteins E6 and E7 are non-self, tumor-specific antigens uniformly expressed in HPV16-associated cancers. Despite their immunogenic potential, immunotherapies mobilizing endogenous T cells, including checkpoint inhibitors and therapeutic vaccines, have yielded suboptimal outcomes. The biological basis for this discrepancy remains incompletely defined. Adoptive cellular therapy using preselected high-avidity T cell receptors (TCRs) targeting E6/E7 has achieved promising clinical responses, but current approaches are largely restricted to HLA-A*02:01. We sought to define the recognition landscape, functional properties, and therapeutic potential of naturally occurring HPV16-reactive TCRs.Methods Reactivity of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) from HPV16-positive tumors to E6/E7 was identified by 4-1BB upregulation following in vitro stimulation (IVS). Reactive CD8+ T cells were isolated and subjected to single-cell TCR sequencing. Candidate TCRs were reconstructed and retrovirally transduced into primary human T cells. Antigen recognition and HLA restriction were determined using COS-7 cells co-expressing individual HLA alleles with full-length E6/E7. Core epitopes were mapped and confirmed by tetramer binding. Functional avidity was assessed by IFN-γ secretion and real-time cytotoxicity against HPV16+ cell lines. Lead TCRs were evaluated in NSG mouse models. Cross-reactivity was assessed via alanine scanning-derived motifs. Multi-HLA TCR combinations and CD8αβ co-engineering strategies were evaluated.Results Sixty TIL specimens from 50 patients were evaluated by IVS. A total of 183 TCRs were reconstructed from 4-1BB + CD8+ T cells isolated from 20 patients. Forty-two TCRs were validated to recognize 17 epitopes across 12 class I HLA alleles, mapping back to 12 of 50 (24%) patients. Endogenous TCR recognition of E6/E7 converged on a limited set of epitope-HLA interfaces, defining a sparse and constrained recognition landscape. Most TCRs showed limited functional avidity, with heterogeneous IFN-γ secretion and incomplete tumor killing. Three rare high-avidity TCRs restricted by HLA-A*02:01, A*33:03, and B*15:01 mediated complete tumor regression in vivo without detectable cross-reactivity. Combinatorial multi-HLA targeting prevented tumor outgrowth driven by HLA loss-of-heterozygosity that evaded single-TCR therapy. CD8αβ co-expression enhanced low-avidity TCR activity and reduced the cell dose required for complete responses with high-avidity TCRs.Conclusions Naturally occurring HPV16-specific T cell immunity is constrained by repertoire gaps, sparse antigen-HLA recognition and generally weak TCR functional avidity. Systematic TCR discovery enables the identification of rare high-performance TCRs capable of mediating potent antitumor activity, providing a rationale for adoptive cell therapy with preselected TCRs. Multi-HLA TCR combinations and CD8αβ engineering offer complementary strategies to improve therapeutic efficacy and limit immune escape.

Despite their immunogenic potential, immunotherapies mobilizing endogenous T cells, including checkpoint inhibitors and therapeutic vaccines, have yielded suboptimal outcomes. The biological basis for this discrepancy remains incompletely defined. Adoptive cellular therapy using preselected high-avidity T cell receptors (TCRs) targeting E6/E7 has achieved promising clinical responses, but current approaches are largely restricted to HLA-A*02:01. We sought to define the recognition landscape, functional properties, and therapeutic potential of naturally occurring HPV16-reactive TCRs.Methods Reactivity of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) from HPV16-positive tumors to E6/E7 was identified by 4-1BB upregulation following in vitro stimulation (IVS). Reactive CD8+ T cells were isolated and subjected to single-cell TCR sequencing. Candidate TCRs were reconstructed and retrovirally transduced into primary human T cells. Antigen recognition and HLA restriction were determined using COS-7 cells co-expressing individual HLA alleles with full-length E6/E7. Core epitopes were mapped and confirmed by tetramer binding. Functional avidity was assessed by IFN-γ secretion and real-time cytotoxicity against HPV16+ cell lines. Lead TCRs were evaluated in NSG mouse models. Cross-reactivity was assessed via alanine scanning-derived motifs. Multi-HLA TCR combinations and CD8αβ co-engineering strategies were evaluated.Results Sixty TIL specimens from 50 patients were evaluated by IVS. A total of 183 TCRs were reconstructed from 4-1BB + CD8+ T cells isolated from 20 patients. Forty-two TCRs were validated to recognize 17 epitopes across 12 class I HLA alleles, mapping back to 12 of 50 (24%) patients. Endogenous TCR recognition of E6/E7 converged on a limited set of epitope-HLA interfaces, defining a sparse and constrained recognition landscape. Most TCRs showed limited functional avidity, with heterogeneous IFN-γ secretion and incomplete tumor killing. Three rare high-avidity TCRs restricted by HLA-A*02:01, A*33:03, and B*15:01 mediated complete tumor regression in vivo without detectable cross-reactivity. Combinatorial multi-HLA targeting prevented tumor outgrowth driven by HLA loss-of-heterozygosity that evaded single-TCR therapy. CD8αβ co-expression enhanced low-avidity TCR activity and reduced the cell dose required for complete responses with high-avidity TCRs.Conclusions Naturally occurring HPV16-specific T cell immunity is constrained by repertoire gaps, sparse antigen-HLA recognition and generally weak TCR functional avidity. Systematic TCR discovery enables the identification of rare high-performance TCRs capable of mediating potent antitumor activity, providing a rationale for adoptive cell therapy with preselected TCRs. Multi-HLA TCR combinations and CD8αβ engineering offer complementary strategies to improve therapeutic efficacy and limit immune escape.

title: HPV-Associated transcriptional landscape in cervical and head and neck cancers
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the principal cause of cervical cancer (CC) and an increasingly significant contributor to head and neck cancer (HNC). Although these malignancies arise at different anatomical sites, they share a common viral aetiology, and the molecular alterations associated with HPV across both cancers remain incompletely understood. The present study aimed to identify transcriptional alterations common to HPV-positive CC and HNC using integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses. Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed on HPV-positive tumours and normal tissues from both cancers to identify shared tumour-associated genes. To distinguish HPV-associated alterations from general tumour-related changes, these genes were further refined by comparison with HPV-positive and HPV-negative tumours in both cancers. The resulting candidate genes were prioritised using a machine learning-based feature selection strategy and subsequently validated in independent transcriptomic cohorts and single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. A total of 52 shared HPV-associated genes were identified by integrating differential expression and co-expression network analyses, of which six genes (CDKN2A, CDKN2B-AS1, MCM2, KCNS1, EFNB3, and COL28A1) were prioritised by machine learning. The six-gene panel consistently distinguished HPV-positive from HPV-negative tumours in both CC and HNC and showed similar expression patterns in independent validation cohorts as well. Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis further demonstrated that these genes were predominantly expressed in epithelial cells, with CDKN2A, CDKN2B-AS1, KCNS1, and MCM2 showing increased expression in HPV-positive samples, whereas EFNB3 and COL28A1 were reduced. These genes are associated with biological processes relevant to tumour progression, including cell-cycle regulation, DNA replication, extracellular matrix organisation and cell–cell communication. Correlation with HPV viral transcript levels revealed modest associations for the identified genes, particularly CDKN2A and MCM2. Shared transcriptional alterations were identified across HPV-associated CC and HNC, providing further insight into the molecular landscape of HPV-driven carcinogenesis. These findings offer a foundation for future studies aimed at understanding HPV-associated tumour biology and identifying potential biomarkers.

title: Smartphone-Based Fluorescence Detection for HPV-Positive Oropharyngeal Carcinoma
abstract: This work presents a low-cost, portable, rapid detection system for screening human papillomavirus (HPV)-related oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. The device uses off-the-shelf components, including a smartphone, a mini heating block (isothermal at 39 °C), a voltage-regulated LED, and a 3D-printed housing. We optimized recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) and a sequence-specific Exo probe targeting the HPV 16 E2 gene for sensitivity and specificity. We excited the RPA reaction tube with a blue LED, and a smartphone captured images to measure fluorescence intensity. A low-cost color film replaced an optical filter. Plots of green-over-blue (G/B) pixel intensities against time showed the expected sigmoidal shapes. The limit of detection (LOD) was 10 pg/μL for plasmid samples, and 1 cell/μL for HPV-positive oropharyngeal cell carcinoma spiked into human saliva, demonstrating excellent sensitivity. Standard curves also showed a strong linear relationship with logarithmic concentrations, with R 2 values of 0.964 for plasmid and 0.872 for carcinoma cells in saliva. The amplification times were <10 minutes for plasmid and <15 minutes for carcinoma cells in saliva. Overall, these results show that the device and method are low-cost, rapid, and simple, showing strong potential as a point-of-care diagnostic tool.
